name: Chicken casserole
notes: A baked casserole of cooked chicken, vegetables, and mushrooms bound in a creamy soup-based sauce and topped with bread or crackers.

name: Broccoli casserole
notes: Broccoli florets baked with eggs, cheese, and a buttery cracker topping — a Southern potluck staple.

name: Banana bread
notes: A moist quick bread sweetened by mashed ripe bananas, with butter, eggs, and flour — typically served sliced.

name: Cheese ball
notes: A blend of cream cheese, shredded cheese, and seasonings shaped into a ball and rolled in chopped nuts — served as an appetizer with crackers.

name: Squash casserole
notes: Sliced yellow squash baked with eggs, cheese, and a buttered cracker topping — a Southern side dish.

name: Zucchini bread
notes: A spiced quick bread folded with grated zucchini — moist, lightly sweet, often with nuts.

name: Chili
notes: Ground beef simmered with tomatoes, beans, peppers, and chili powder until thick — the American bowl-of-red.

name: Meatloaf
notes: Ground beef mixed with breadcrumbs, egg, and onion, baked in a loaf shape and glazed with ketchup — a diner classic.

name: Baked beans
notes: Navy beans slow-baked with bacon, molasses, brown sugar, and mustard in a tomato sauce — a barbecue side.

name: Fruit salad
notes: Diced fresh fruit tossed together — sometimes with whipped topping or marshmallows in the American picnic style.

name: Pumpkin bread
notes: A spiced quick bread made with pumpkin puree, eggs, oil, and warm spices — moist and lightly sweet.

name: Carrot cake
notes: A spiced layer cake with grated carrots, oil, and walnuts, topped with cream cheese frosting.

name: Corn casserole
notes: A spoon-bread-style bake of corn kernels, cream-style corn, eggs, butter, and sour cream — sweet, custardy, almost pudding-like.

name: Cranberry salad
notes: A holiday gelatin salad of cranberries, pineapple, and other fruit set in sweetened gelatin — a Thanksgiving side.

name: Potato casserole
notes: Hash browns or sliced potatoes baked with sour cream, cheese, and cream of chicken soup, topped with butter or crushed crackers.

name: Chocolate chip cookies
notes: Drop cookies of brown-and-white sugar butter dough studded with semisweet chocolate chips — the Toll House standard.

name: Broccoli salad
notes: Raw broccoli florets tossed with bacon, cheese, raisins, and red onion in a sweet-tangy mayonnaise dressing.

name: Brownies
notes: A dense fudgy chocolate bar baked with butter, eggs, cocoa or melted chocolate, sugar, and flour — cut into squares.

name: Banana nut bread
notes: Banana bread with chopped walnuts or pecans folded into the batter.

name: Sweet potato casserole
notes: Mashed sweet potatoes baked under a brown-sugar-and-pecan streusel or toasted-marshmallow topping — a Southern Thanksgiving side.

name: Taco salad
notes: Seasoned ground beef and beans over lettuce with cheese, tomatoes, and crushed tortilla chips in a creamy salsa-mayo dressing.

name: Apple crisp
notes: Spiced sliced apples baked under a crunchy oat-and-butter streusel topping — served warm, often with ice cream.

name: Sugar cookies
notes: Rolled or drop cookies of sweet butter dough — crisp at the edges, often glazed or sprinkled.

name: Peanut butter pie
notes: A no-bake pie of peanut butter whipped with cream cheese and folded into whipped topping, set in a graham or chocolate-cookie crust.

name: Peach cobbler
notes: Sliced peaches baked under a buttery cake or biscuit topping — a Southern dessert served warm with ice cream.

name: Peanut butter fudge
notes: A no-cook fudge of peanut butter, sugar, butter, and milk cooked to soft-ball, beaten, and poured to set.

name: Beef stroganoff
notes: Strips of beef sautéed with mushrooms and onion in a sour-cream-and-mustard sauce, served over egg noodles.

name: Sausage balls
notes: Bite-size baked balls of breakfast sausage, shredded cheddar, and biscuit mix — a Southern appetizer.

name: Corn pudding
notes: Sweet corn kernels baked in a custard of eggs, milk, sugar, and butter — soft-set and lightly sweet.

name: Breakfast casserole
notes: A make-ahead bake of bread or hash browns layered with sausage, eggs, milk, and cheese — set overnight and baked in the morning.

name: Strawberry pie
notes: A pre-baked crust filled with fresh strawberries set in a sweet glaze — chilled and served with whipped cream.

name: Green bean casserole
notes: Green beans baked in cream-of-mushroom soup with milk and topped with crispy fried onions — the Campbell's Thanksgiving side.

name: Potato soup
notes: Diced potatoes simmered in broth with onion and milk or cream, finished with butter and herbs.

name: Dump cake
notes: Canned fruit pie filling topped with a dry yellow-cake mix and pats of butter, baked until golden — no mixing required.

name: Spinach dip
notes: Chopped spinach mixed with sour cream, mayo, and a packet of soup mix — served cold in a hollowed bread bowl.

name: Fresh apple cake
notes: A spiced oil-based cake folded with chopped fresh apples and nuts — moist and tender.

name: Banana pudding
notes: Layers of vanilla pudding, sliced bananas, and vanilla wafers, topped with whipped cream or meringue — a Southern icebox dessert.

name: Monkey bread
notes: Pieces of biscuit dough rolled in cinnamon sugar, layered in a Bundt pan, and baked with a brown-sugar-butter glaze — pulled apart by hand.

name: Potato salad
notes: Boiled potatoes tossed with mayo, mustard, chopped eggs, celery, pickles, and onion — chilled and served as a picnic side.

name: Chocolate pie
notes: A pre-baked pastry shell filled with a cooked chocolate pudding or custard and topped with whipped cream or meringue.

name: Oatmeal cookies
notes: Drop cookies of oats, butter, brown sugar, and spices — often with raisins or chocolate chips folded in.

name: Macaroni and cheese
notes: Elbow macaroni in a cheddar-bechamel sauce, often baked with a buttered breadcrumb topping — the American comfort classic.

name: Fudge
notes: A dense sugar-and-cream confection cooked to soft-ball, beaten until creamy, and poured to set — usually chocolate flavored.

name: Shrimp dip
notes: Cream cheese whipped with chopped shrimp, lemon, and seasonings — served chilled with crackers.

name: Party punch
notes: A non-alcoholic party drink of fruit juices and ginger ale or sherbet, served from a punch bowl over ice.

name: Spaghetti meat sauce
notes: A long-simmered tomato sauce with ground beef, onions, peppers, and Italian herbs — served over spaghetti.

name: Chicken salad
notes: Chopped cooked chicken tossed with mayo, celery, grapes, and nuts — served as a sandwich filling or over greens.

name: Taco dip
notes: Layers of refried beans or seasoned cream cheese with sour cream, salsa, shredded cheese, lettuce, and olives — served cold with tortilla chips.

name: Chocolate cake
notes: A layer or sheet cake of cocoa-based butter or oil batter, frosted with chocolate buttercream or ganache.

name: Scalloped potatoes
notes: Sliced potatoes layered with onions and baked in a cream-and-cheese sauce until tender and golden on top.

name: Banana split cake
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of graham-cracker crust, whipped cream cheese filling, sliced bananas, crushed pineapple, and whipped topping with cherries.

name: Fruit dip
notes: A sweet cream-cheese-and-marshmallow-fluff dip served chilled with sliced fresh fruit.

name: Pasta salad
notes: Cooked pasta tossed with chopped vegetables, cheese, and Italian or mayo-based dressing — served cold.

name: Zucchini casserole
notes: Sliced zucchini baked with onions, sour cream, and shredded cheese under a buttered cracker or stuffing topping.

name: Chicken enchiladas
notes: Tortillas rolled around shredded chicken and cheese, lined in a baking dish, covered in red or green chile sauce and more cheese, and baked.

name: Vegetable casserole
notes: A mix of vegetables baked with cheese and a buttery cracker or breadcrumb topping.

name: Sweet potato pie
notes: A custard pie of mashed sweet potato, eggs, evaporated milk, and warm spices in a butter crust — a Southern Thanksgiving classic.

name: Rice pudding
notes: Cooked rice simmered slowly in milk and sugar with vanilla and cinnamon — served warm or chilled.

name: Caramel corn
notes: Popped corn coated in a hot caramel of butter, brown sugar, and corn syrup, then baked until crisp.

name: Macaroni salad
notes: Elbow macaroni tossed with mayo, mustard, chopped celery, onion, pickle, and hard-boiled egg — chilled as a picnic side.

name: Hot chicken salad
notes: Chopped cooked chicken bound with mayo and lemon, mixed with celery and almonds, topped with cheese and crushed potato chips, and baked until bubbling.

name: Coconut pie
notes: A custard pie of eggs, milk, sugar, and shredded coconut — sometimes self-crusting (impossible pie) without a separate pastry shell.

name: Hamburger casserole
notes: Browned ground beef baked with potatoes or noodles, vegetables, and shredded cheese under a tomato or cream-soup sauce.

name: Mexican cornbread
notes: A skillet cornbread loaded with jalapeños, cheddar cheese, corn kernels, and sometimes onion or peppers — savory and rich.

name: Mexican casserole
notes: Layered tortillas, seasoned meat, salsa, beans, and cheese baked together — a homestyle Tex-Mex one-dish meal.

name: Sloppy joes
notes: Ground beef simmered in a sweet-tangy tomato-and-ketchup sauce with onions and peppers, served piled on soft hamburger buns.

name: Stuffed mushrooms
notes: Mushroom caps filled with a mixture of sausage or breadcrumbs, herbs, and Parmesan, then baked until golden.

name: Hush puppies
notes: Small balls of cornmeal batter with onion, deep-fried until crisp — a Southern fish-fry side.

name: Cheesecake
notes: A baked or no-bake dessert of sweetened cream cheese set on a graham-cracker crust — dense and tangy.

name: Chicken divan
notes: Cooked chicken and steamed broccoli baked in a sherry-and-curry-laced cream sauce topped with cheese and breadcrumbs.

name: Chicken and rice
notes: Chicken pieces baked or simmered with rice in a seasoned broth or cream-soup sauce until both are tender.

name: Blueberry muffins
notes: Tender muffins studded with fresh or frozen blueberries, often topped with a sugar streusel.

name: Taco soup
notes: Ground beef simmered with diced tomatoes, beans, corn, and taco seasoning — a soupy chili-style one-pot.

name: Chicken spaghetti
notes: Cooked spaghetti tossed with shredded chicken, peppers, onions, and Velveeta-style cheese sauce, then baked until bubbly.

name: Watergate salad
notes: A green fluffy salad-dessert of pistachio pudding mix, crushed pineapple, miniature marshmallows, and Cool Whip with chopped pecans.

name: Tuna casserole
notes: Cooked egg noodles baked with canned tuna, cream of mushroom soup, peas, and cheese, topped with crushed potato chips or breadcrumbs.

name: Fruit pizza
notes: A sugar-cookie crust spread with sweetened cream cheese and topped with sliced fresh fruit and a citrus glaze.

name: Applesauce cake
notes: A spiced cake made moist with applesauce, often with raisins and walnuts folded in — a classic depression-era bake.

name: Spanish rice
notes: Long-grain rice toasted in oil, then simmered with tomato sauce, onions, peppers, and broth — Tex-Mex rather than Iberian despite the name.

name: Hash brown casserole
notes: Frozen shredded hash browns baked with cream of chicken soup, sour cream, and shredded cheese under a cornflake topping — the "funeral potatoes" classic.

name: Vegetable dip
notes: A sour-cream-and-mayo dip seasoned with dried herbs, garlic, and onion — served chilled with raw vegetables.

name: No-bake cookies
notes: Cocoa, sugar, milk, and butter cooked to a fudge, then stirred with peanut butter and oats and dropped onto wax paper to set.

name: Dirt cake
notes: A layered no-bake dessert of crushed chocolate cookies, vanilla pudding mixed with cream cheese and whipped topping — served in a flowerpot for novelty.

name: Peanut butter balls
notes: No-bake balls of peanut butter, powdered sugar, and butter rolled and dipped in melted chocolate — buckeye-style.

name: Tater tot casserole
notes: Ground beef and vegetables baked under a layer of frozen tater tots with cream of mushroom soup and shredded cheese — a Midwestern hot-dish.

name: Chicken pot pie
notes: Diced chicken and vegetables in a creamy gravy baked under a flaky pastry crust.

name: Chicken and dumplings
notes: Chicken simmered in broth with vegetables, finished with soft dough dumplings dropped on top to steam-cook.

name: Vegetable soup
notes: A clear-broth soup of mixed vegetables — sometimes with ground beef and tomato — simmered until tender.

name: Buttermilk pie
notes: A Southern custard pie of buttermilk, eggs, sugar, butter, and a touch of flour — tangy and silky in a flaky shell.

name: Vegetable pizza
notes: A cold "pizza" of crescent-roll crust spread with herbed cream cheese and topped with chopped raw vegetables and shredded cheese.

name: Coconut cake
notes: A white layer cake brushed with coconut milk and frosted with cream-cheese or buttercream icing, covered in shredded coconut.

name: French onion soup
notes: Slow-caramelized onions simmered in beef broth with wine and herbs, topped with a toasted bread round and broiled with melted Gruyère.

name: Pizza casserole
notes: Cooked pasta layered with ground beef, pepperoni, marinara, and mozzarella, baked until bubbly — pizza flavors in a casserole.

name: Angel biscuits
notes: A tender Southern biscuit leavened with both yeast and baking powder for an exceptionally light, fluffy rise.

name: Snickerdoodles
notes: Soft butter cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar before baking, with a slight tang from cream of tartar.

name: Cornbread
notes: A quick bread of cornmeal, flour, eggs, and milk, baked in a hot skillet or pan — Southern style is unsweetened and crisp-edged.

name: Cabbage casserole
notes: Shredded cabbage baked with ground beef, tomato, and cheese — a deconstructed cabbage-roll bake.

name: Guacamole
notes: Mashed ripe avocado mixed with lime, salt, onion, jalapeño, and cilantro — served with tortilla chips.

name: Lasagna
notes: Layered pasta sheets with ricotta, ground beef in tomato sauce, and melted mozzarella, baked until bubbly.

name: Ice cream
notes: A frozen custard of milk, cream, eggs, sugar, and vanilla churned in an ice-cream maker until set.

name: Punch bowl cake
notes: A layered trifle of cubed cake, pudding, fruit, and whipped topping assembled in a glass punch bowl.

name: Chicken tetrazzini
notes: Cooked spaghetti or linguine baked with chicken, mushrooms, and a sherry-cream sauce under a Parmesan and breadcrumb topping.

name: Strawberry pretzel salad
notes: A layered dessert of crushed-pretzel crust, sweet whipped cream cheese, and strawberry gelatin with fresh strawberries — salty-sweet.

name: Spaghetti salad
notes: Cold cooked spaghetti tossed with Italian dressing, chopped vegetables, olives, and Parmesan — a picnic pasta variant.

name: Strawberry salad
notes: Sliced strawberries layered with whipped cream or yogurt and toasted nuts — sometimes set with gelatin.

name: Strawberry cake
notes: A pink layer cake made from white cake mix and strawberry gelatin with fresh or frozen strawberries folded in.

name: Artichoke dip
notes: Chopped artichoke hearts mixed with mayo, sour cream, and Parmesan, baked until bubbly — served hot with crackers or bread.

name: Dinner rolls
notes: Soft yeasted rolls of enriched dough — pulled-apart and served warm with butter at dinner.

name: Pepper steak
notes: Strips of beef stir-fried with sliced bell peppers and onions in a soy-and-ginger sauce, served over rice.

name: Bran muffins
notes: High-fiber muffins of wheat bran, flour, buttermilk or molasses, and often raisins — moist and slightly sweet.

name: Chicken and rice casserole
notes: Raw rice and chicken pieces baked together with cream of mushroom soup and a packet of onion soup mix until rice absorbs the broth.

name: Broccoli cornbread
notes: A skillet cornbread enriched with chopped broccoli, cottage cheese, and butter — a moist, savory side.

name: Cream cheese pound cake
notes: A dense, fine-crumb pound cake made tender by a block of cream cheese beaten into the butter-and-sugar base.

name: Pork chop casserole
notes: Bone-in pork chops baked over rice or sliced potatoes in cream of mushroom soup.

name: Lemon pie
notes: A pre-baked crust filled with tangy lemon custard and topped with meringue or whipped cream — typically lemon meringue or icebox style.

name: Chicken cacciatore
notes: Bone-in chicken braised hunter-style in tomatoes, peppers, mushrooms, onions, and wine with herbs.

name: Crab dip
notes: Lump crab mixed with cream cheese, mayo, lemon, and Old Bay — served hot or cold with crackers or crostini.

name: Deviled eggs
notes: Hard-boiled eggs halved and filled with a yolk paste of mayo, mustard, and seasonings — dusted with paprika.

name: Mexican cornbread (variant)
notes: Cornbread baked with cheddar, creamed corn, and chopped jalapeños — slightly sweeter than the skillet-Tex-Mex version.

name: Stuffed peppers
notes: Bell peppers hollowed and filled with seasoned ground beef and rice in tomato sauce, baked until tender.

name: Swiss steak
notes: Round steak pounded thin, dredged in flour, browned, then braised slowly with onions and tomato until fork-tender.

name: Mexican chicken
notes: Cooked chicken layered with tortilla chips, salsa, peppers, and cheese, baked into a Tex-Mex casserole.

name: Asparagus casserole
notes: Canned or fresh asparagus baked with hard-boiled eggs, cheese, and mushroom soup under a cracker-crumb topping.

name: Cinnamon rolls
notes: Yeasted dough rolled around butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon, sliced into spirals, baked, and drizzled with sweet glaze or cream-cheese frosting.

name: Cornbread (skillet)
notes: A skillet-baked quick bread of cornmeal, eggs, milk, and a little flour — slightly sweet in the Northern style, savory in the Southern.

name: German potato salad
notes: Sliced warm potatoes tossed with crisp bacon, onions, and a tangy bacon-fat-and-vinegar dressing — served warm rather than cold.

name: Oatmeal cake
notes: A spiced cake made with oatmeal soaked in hot water, topped with a broiled brown-sugar-coconut-pecan glaze.

name: Meatballs
notes: Ground beef mixed with breadcrumbs, egg, and seasonings, rolled and baked or browned, then simmered in tomato or cream sauce.

name: Taco casserole
notes: Layered casserole of seasoned ground beef, tortilla chips, salsa, beans, and shredded cheese — baked until bubbly.

name: Mexican layer dip
notes: A cold layered dip of refried beans, sour cream and seasonings, salsa, cheese, lettuce, and olives — served with tortilla chips.

name: Chocolate pound cake
notes: A dense pound cake enriched with cocoa or melted chocolate, baked in a tube or loaf pan and often glazed.

name: Buttermilk biscuits
notes: A flaky Southern quick bread of flour, baking powder, cold butter or shortening, and buttermilk — cut and baked until risen.

name: Sauerkraut salad
notes: Drained sauerkraut tossed with chopped peppers, onion, celery, and a sweet vinegar dressing — chilled overnight.

name: Turtle cake
notes: Chocolate cake layered with caramel sauce, chopped pecans, and chocolate chips — turtle-candy flavors baked into a sheet cake.

name: Shrimp creole
notes: Shrimp simmered in a Louisiana sauce of tomatoes, peppers, onion, celery, and Creole seasoning, served over rice.

name: Sausage casserole
notes: Breakfast sausage browned and baked with eggs, milk, bread or rice, cheese, and vegetables — a hearty one-dish meal.

name: Enchilada casserole
notes: A layered "stacked" enchilada bake of tortillas, seasoned meat, enchilada sauce, and cheese — easier than rolling.

name: Spinach balls
notes: Bite-size baked balls of chopped spinach, herbed stuffing mix, eggs, butter, and Parmesan — a freezer-friendly appetizer.

name: Fried rice
notes: Day-old cold rice stir-fried with eggs, scallions, peas and carrots, soy sauce, and often diced meat — fast wok-style.

name: Chess pie
notes: A Southern custard pie of butter, sugar, eggs, and a touch of cornmeal or flour — translucent and rich.

name: Fruit cocktail cake
notes: A one-bowl sheet cake folded with canned fruit cocktail and its syrup, often with a brown-sugar-coconut broiled topping.

name: Spinach salad
notes: Baby spinach with crisp bacon, sliced mushrooms, hard-boiled egg, and red onion in a sweet warm bacon dressing.

name: Strawberry bread
notes: A spiced quick bread folded with chopped fresh or frozen strawberries — moist and lightly sweet, often with nuts.

name: Earthquake cake
notes: A German-chocolate-style sheet cake with coconut and pecans on the bottom and a cream-cheese-and-powdered-sugar layer that swirls down through the batter while baking.

name: Pineapple casserole
notes: Canned pineapple chunks baked with sharp cheddar, sugar, and a buttery cracker topping — a Southern sweet-savory side.

name: Corn chowder
notes: Sweet corn simmered in a milk-or-cream base with diced potatoes, onion, and bacon until thickened.

name: Spinach casserole
notes: Chopped spinach baked in a custard with cream cheese, eggs, and butter under a Parmesan or cheddar top.

name: Banana cake
notes: A soft layer or sheet cake of mashed bananas, butter, sugar, and eggs — often frosted with cream-cheese icing.

name: Breakfast pizza
notes: A crescent-roll or pizza-dough crust topped with scrambled eggs, breakfast sausage or bacon, cheese, and sometimes hash browns — baked until set.

name: Pumpkin cake
notes: A spiced oil-based cake of pumpkin puree, eggs, and warm spices, usually frosted with cream cheese icing.

name: Frozen fruit salad
notes: Mixed canned and fresh fruit folded with sweetened cream cheese and whipped topping, frozen in a pan and sliced — a retro Southern picnic dessert.

name: Scalloped corn
notes: Sweet corn baked in a custard of eggs, milk, and butter under a buttered cracker topping.

name: Marinated carrots
notes: Blanched carrot slices tossed with peppers and onions in a sweet tomato-vinegar marinade — chilled overnight as a Southern side.

name: Classic meatloaf
notes: A ground-beef loaf bound with breadcrumbs and egg, seasoned with onions and herbs, glazed with ketchup, and baked.

name: Russian tea
notes: A powdered hot-drink mix of instant tea, Tang, sugar, and warm spices — stirred into hot water; non-alcoholic despite the name.

name: Yeast rolls
notes: Soft enriched yeasted rolls of flour, milk, butter, sugar, and egg — proofed twice and baked until golden.

name: Chocolate fudge
notes: Sugar, butter, chocolate, and evaporated milk cooked to soft-ball and beaten until creamy — poured to set and cut into squares.

name: Coleslaw
notes: Shredded cabbage and carrot in a sweet-tangy mayonnaise dressing — the picnic-and-barbecue staple.

name: Cucumber salad
notes: Thinly sliced cucumber and onion tossed in a sweet vinegar dressing — chilled until crisp.

name: Roast chicken
notes: Seasoned whole chicken or pieces roasted with vegetables — the unadorned baseline preparation.

name: Party punch
notes: A non-alcoholic gathering drink of mixed juices, ginger ale, and sherbet — ladled from a bowl over ice.

name: Pineapple cake
notes: A moist cake folded with crushed pineapple in its juice, often glazed with cream cheese frosting.

name: Dill dip
notes: Sour cream and mayo seasoned with dill, parsley, onion, and Beau Monde — served chilled with vegetables or bread.

name: Quiche
notes: A pastry shell filled with an egg-and-cream custard, cheese, and vegetables or bacon — baked until just set.

name: Corn fritters
notes: Sweet corn folded into a leavened batter and pan-fried in spoonfuls until crisp and golden.

name: Jello salad
notes: A molded Southern dessert-salad of fruit-flavored gelatin set with canned pineapple, cream cheese, and sometimes marshmallows.

name: Lemon bars
notes: A shortbread crust topped with a baked lemon-egg curd, cooled and dusted with powdered sugar.

name: Seven-layer salad
notes: Lettuce, peas, onion, bacon, cheese, and other layers built in a glass bowl, sealed under a mayo-sugar topping, and chilled overnight.

name: Eggplant casserole
notes: Sliced eggplant baked with eggs, milk, cheese, and a buttered cracker topping — a Southern-style side.

name: Salmon loaf
notes: Canned salmon mixed with breadcrumbs, egg, milk, lemon, and onion, baked in a loaf — a Depression-era pantry dish.

name: Pot roast
notes: A tough beef cut (chuck or round) seared and slow-braised in broth with onions, carrots, and potatoes until fork-tender.

name: Cream of broccoli soup
notes: Broccoli simmered in chicken broth, pureed, and thickened with a milk-and-butter roux.

name: Sweet and sour chicken
notes: Battered chicken chunks deep-fried and tossed in a glossy sauce of vinegar, sugar, ketchup, and pineapple — served over rice.

name: Granola
notes: Rolled oats baked with honey or maple, oil, nuts, seeds, and dried fruit until clustery and crisp.

name: Layered salad
notes: A bowl-built salad of lettuce, peas, eggs, cheese, and bacon under a mayonnaise-and-sugar seal, chilled overnight — a variant of seven-layer.

name: Rice casserole
notes: Raw rice baked with broth, beef or mushrooms, and butter until tender — the consommé-rice pantry side.

name: Puppy chow (muddy buddies)
notes: Chex cereal coated in melted chocolate and peanut butter, then tossed with powdered sugar — a sweet snack mix.

name: Jambalaya
notes: A Creole one-pot rice dish with andouille, chicken, shrimp, the holy trinity of vegetables, and Cajun seasoning.

name: Broccoli soup
notes: Broccoli florets simmered with onion and broth, sometimes blended, sometimes left chunky — finished with milk or cream.

name: Hot chocolate mix
notes: A dry pantry mix of powdered milk, cocoa, sugar, and powdered creamer — stirred into hot water for instant cocoa.

name: Calico beans
notes: A baked-bean medley of kidney, butter, and pork-and-beans simmered with ground beef, bacon, brown sugar, and barbecue sauce.

name: Cauliflower salad
notes: Raw cauliflower florets tossed with bacon, cheese, and red onion in a sweet mayonnaise dressing — broccoli-salad style.

name: Gingerbread
notes: A dark spiced quick bread or cake leavened with baking soda and sweetened with molasses — served warm with whipped cream or lemon sauce.

name: Fruitcake
notes: A dense holiday cake packed with candied fruit, dried fruit, and nuts in a spiced butter batter — often soaked in spirits and aged.

name: Irish soda bread
notes: A quick bread of flour, buttermilk, and baking soda — sometimes sweetened with raisins, baked as a round loaf with a deep cross slashed on top.

name: New England clam chowder
notes: Diced potatoes and clams simmered in a salt-pork-and-onion base, finished with milk and cream — the chowder house classic.

name: Red beans and rice
notes: Red beans slow-simmered with andouille sausage and the holy trinity, served over long-grain rice — a New Orleans Monday standard.

name: Fresh strawberry pie
notes: Whole or sliced fresh strawberries piled in a baked crust and set with a cooked sugar-and-cornstarch glaze — chilled and served with whipped cream.

name: Pizza
notes: A yeasted dough crust topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and toppings (commonly pepperoni or sausage), baked at high heat.

name: Enchiladas
notes: Corn tortillas dipped in chile sauce, rolled around a meat-or-cheese filling, baked, and topped with more sauce and crumbled cheese.

name: Lemon squares
notes: A shortbread crust topped with a baked tart lemon custard — cut into squares and dusted with powdered sugar.

name: Broccoli and rice casserole
notes: Cooked rice baked with broccoli florets, cream of mushroom soup, Cheez Whiz or processed cheese, and butter — a Southern potluck mainstay.

name: Coconut cream pie
notes: A baked pastry shell filled with a coconut-milk custard pudding, topped with whipped cream and toasted coconut.

name: Spaghetti pie
notes: Cooked spaghetti pressed into a pie pan with egg and Parmesan as the "crust", filled with ricotta and meat sauce and baked.

name: Hummingbird cake
notes: A spiced banana-pineapple layer cake with chopped pecans, frosted with cream cheese icing — a Southern classic.

name: Orange salad
notes: A molded gelatin salad of mandarin oranges, crushed pineapple, and cottage cheese set with orange Jello.

name: Mississippi mud cake
notes: A dense chocolate sheet cake topped with marshmallow creme and a layer of chocolate-pecan frosting — gooey and rich.

name: Crab cakes
notes: Lump crab bound with mayo, egg, and a little breadcrumb or cracker, formed into patties and pan-fried or broiled.

name: Blueberry salad
notes: A molded gelatin salad of blueberries and crushed pineapple topped with a sour cream and cream cheese layer — a Southern potluck dish.

name: Potato chip cookies
notes: A butter shortbread-style cookie with crushed potato chips and chopped pecans folded into the dough — salty-sweet and crunchy.

name: Pistachio salad
notes: Crushed pineapple folded with instant pistachio pudding mix, miniature marshmallows, and whipped topping — the green "Watergate" cousin.

name: Southern tea cakes
notes: A simple sugar-butter cookie scented with vanilla and nutmeg — soft, cake-like, traditionally served with tea.

name: Baked corn
notes: Corn kernels baked in a sweet milk-and-egg custard with butter — a Pennsylvania Dutch side dish.

name: Fried green tomatoes
notes: Slices of unripe green tomatoes dredged in egg and cornmeal, then pan-fried until crisp — a Southern summer side.

name: Brunswick stew
notes: A thick Southern stew of pulled pork, chicken, lima beans, corn, potatoes, and tomato in barbecue-spiced broth.

name: Chicken noodle soup
notes: Chicken simmered in broth with carrots, celery, onion, and egg noodles — the home-remedy classic.

name: Marinated vegetable salad
notes: Mixed cooked or canned vegetables tossed in a sweet vinaigrette and chilled overnight — a make-ahead picnic side.

name: Divinity
notes: A white, fluffy confection of hot sugar syrup whipped into stiff egg whites with vanilla and pecans — dropped onto wax paper to set.

name: Cabbage rolls
notes: Blanched cabbage leaves wrapped around ground beef, rice, and onion, then baked in tomato sauce — Eastern European golabki style.

name: Pineapple upside-down cake
notes: A skillet cake baked over pineapple rings and maraschino cherries set in a brown-sugar-butter glaze, inverted to serve.

name: Italian cream cake
notes: A Southern layer cake of buttermilk batter folded with coconut and pecans, frosted with cream cheese icing — despite the name, an American creation.

name: Pea salad
notes: Sweet green peas tossed with hard-boiled egg, cheddar, red onion, and bacon in a mayo dressing — a Southern picnic side.

name: Cheese dip
notes: Velveeta-style processed cheese melted with diced tomatoes and chiles (Rotel) — served warm with tortilla chips.

name: Sweet and sour meatballs
notes: Pan-fried meatballs simmered in a sweet-tangy sauce of vinegar, brown sugar, and pineapple — served over rice or as an appetizer.

name: Vanilla ice cream
notes: A churned custard of milk, cream, sugar, egg yolks, and vanilla — the baseline frozen dessert.

name: Poppy seed cake
notes: A pound-style cake folded with poppy seeds — sometimes lemon-glazed, sometimes baked from a mix with pudding stirred in.

name: Popcorn balls
notes: Popped corn pressed into balls with a hot caramel or marshmallow syrup — a Halloween-and-fair treat.

name: Cheese straws
notes: A short crisp savory biscuit of butter, sharp cheddar, flour, and cayenne — piped into thin straws and baked.

name: Pumpkin cookies
notes: Soft drop cookies of pumpkin puree, butter, brown sugar, and warm spices — often with raisins or a maple glaze.

name: Veg-All casserole
notes: Canned Veg-All mixed vegetables baked with mayo, onion, and shredded cheese under a buttered cracker topping.

name: Refrigerator rolls
notes: A make-ahead enriched yeast dough mixed and chilled overnight, then shaped and baked the next day for soft dinner rolls.

name: Baked chicken
notes: Bone-in chicken pieces seasoned and roasted in a hot oven until skin is crisp and juices run clear.

name: Cherry salad
notes: A molded cherry-gelatin salad set with crushed pineapple, condensed milk, and chopped pecans — a Southern picnic dessert.

name: Cherry delight
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of graham crust, sweet cream cheese, cherry pie filling, and whipped topping.

name: Orange Julius
notes: Frozen orange juice concentrate, milk, sugar, vanilla, and ice blended into a frothy creamsicle-flavored drink.

name: Spiced tea
notes: Black tea simmered with orange juice, cinnamon sticks, and cloves — sweetened and served hot.

name: Molasses cookies
notes: Soft chewy cookies of butter, molasses, brown sugar, and warm spices — rolled in sugar before baking.

name: Three-bean salad
notes: Green, wax, and kidney beans tossed with onion and peppers in a sweet vinegar dressing — chilled overnight.

name: Lemon meringue pie
notes: A baked crust filled with tangy lemon custard and topped with billows of sweetened meringue, browned in the oven.

name: Million dollar pie
notes: A no-bake pie of sweetened condensed milk whipped with lemon juice and folded with crushed pineapple, pecans, and whipped topping — in a graham crust.

name: Impossible pie
notes: A blender custard of eggs, milk, sugar, butter, coconut, and Bisquick that self-separates into crust and filling as it bakes.

name: Poppy seed bread
notes: A sweet quick bread folded with poppy seeds and finished with a citrus glaze.

name: Chocolate delight
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan-shortbread crust, sweet cream cheese, chocolate pudding, and whipped topping.

name: Sweet potato souffle
notes: Mashed sweet potato whipped with eggs, sugar, butter, and milk, baked under a brown-sugar-pecan or marshmallow topping.

name: Hot crab dip
notes: Cream cheese, mayo, and lump crab seasoned with Worcestershire and Old Bay, baked until bubbling and served with crackers.

name: Tamale pie
notes: A seasoned beef-and-corn-chili filling topped with cornbread batter and baked — a one-pan Tex-Mex casserole.

name: Hamburger pie
notes: Browned ground beef and vegetables in a savory base, topped with mashed potatoes and cheese, baked like a shepherd's pie.

name: Taco pie
notes: Seasoned ground beef baked over a crescent-roll or cornmeal crust, topped with sour cream, cheese, tomatoes, and crushed chips.

name: Waldorf salad
notes: Diced apples, celery, and walnuts tossed in mayonnaise — sometimes with grapes or raisins; named for the Waldorf-Astoria.

name: Oven-fried chicken
notes: Chicken pieces dredged in seasoned flour or cornflake crumbs and baked on a buttered sheet — a lighter take on fried chicken.

name: Pumpkin roll
notes: A thin pumpkin sponge cake baked on a sheet pan, rolled with a cream-cheese filling, chilled and sliced into pinwheels.

name: Copper pennies
notes: Sliced cooked carrots ("pennies") tossed with bell pepper and onion in a tangy tomato-soup-and-vinegar marinade — chilled overnight.

name: Tuna noodle casserole
notes: Egg noodles baked with canned tuna, peas, and cream of mushroom soup under a buttered breadcrumb or crushed-potato-chip topping.

name: Cheesy potatoes
notes: Frozen hash browns baked with sour cream, cream of chicken soup, and shredded cheddar — a potluck staple also called funeral potatoes.

name: Chocolate eclair cake
notes: A no-bake icebox cake of graham crackers layered with vanilla pudding, topped with chocolate frosting — softens to cake-like texture overnight.

name: Poppy seed chicken
notes: Shredded chicken baked in sour cream and cream of chicken soup under a buttery Ritz-cracker-and-poppy-seed topping.

name: Chocolate chip cake
notes: A Bundt-style cake made from yellow cake mix with sour cream, chocolate chips, and a swirl of cinnamon-sugar.

name: Monster cookies
notes: Oversized drop cookies of peanut butter, oats, M&Ms, and chocolate chips — often flourless and chewy.

name: Buttermilk biscuits (Southern)
notes: A flaky quick bread of flour, baking powder, cold butter or shortening, and buttermilk — patted, cut, and baked until tall.

name: Cornbread salad
notes: Crumbled cornbread layered with beans, tomatoes, cheese, bacon, and ranch-style dressing in a glass bowl — a Southern potluck dish.

name: Salisbury steak
notes: A seasoned ground-beef patty shaped like a steak, pan-fried, then simmered in a mushroom-and-onion brown gravy.

name: Fudge pie
notes: A thin crustless chocolate pie of butter, sugar, eggs, cocoa, and flour — brownie-like with a glossy top.

name: Chocolate mousse
notes: Melted chocolate folded with whipped cream and beaten egg whites or yolks into an airy chilled dessert.

name: Mexican lasagna
notes: Layered tortillas, seasoned ground beef, enchilada or salsa sauce, beans, and cheese — baked into a lasagna-style casserole.

name: Hamburger soup
notes: Ground beef simmered with mixed vegetables, tomatoes, and herbs in beef broth — a stockpot weeknight soup.

name: Texas chocolate sheet cake
notes: A thin chocolate-buttermilk sheet cake topped warm with a poured cocoa-pecan icing that sets to a fudge-like crust.

name: Carrot raisin salad
notes: Shredded carrots tossed with raisins, crushed pineapple, and a mayonnaise-and-sugar dressing — chilled before serving.

name: Salmon patties
notes: Canned salmon mixed with egg, onion, and crushed crackers or cornmeal, formed into patties and pan-fried until crisp.

name: Corn salad
notes: Sweet corn kernels tossed with bell pepper, red onion, and tomato in a vinaigrette — a summer picnic side.

name: Tortilla soup
notes: A spiced tomato-chicken broth with onion, garlic, and chiles, served over crispy tortilla strips and topped with avocado, cheese, and lime.

name: Lentil soup
notes: Brown or green lentils simmered with onions, carrots, celery, and herbs in broth — sometimes with bacon or ham hock.

name: Broccoli cheese soup
notes: Broccoli simmered in a milk-and-roux base, blended with sharp cheddar and Velveeta — a Panera-style chowder.

name: Buckeyes
notes: Peanut butter and powdered sugar balls partially dipped in chocolate to resemble the buckeye nut — an Ohio holiday candy.

name: Chocolate oatmeal cookies
notes: A no-bake cookie of cocoa, sugar, milk, butter, and peanut butter cooked to fudge stage, then stirred with oats and dropped to set.

name: Prune cake
notes: A spiced buttermilk cake folded with cooked pureed prunes and walnuts, often glazed with a buttermilk-soda icing.

name: Chicken broccoli casserole
notes: Cooked chicken and steamed broccoli baked in a mayo, lemon, and cream-of-chicken-soup sauce under a buttered breadcrumb and cheese top.

name: Hash brown potato casserole
notes: A variant of cheesy hash-brown casserole baked with sour cream, cream of chicken soup, cheese, and a buttery cornflake topping.

name: Fruit cobbler
notes: Sweetened fruit baked under a tender biscuit or batter topping — served warm with ice cream.

name: Ham loaf
notes: Ground ham mixed with ground pork, crackers, milk, and egg, baked in a loaf with a sweet brown-sugar mustard glaze — a Pennsylvania Dutch dish.

name: Black bean soup
notes: Black beans simmered with onion, garlic, cumin, and broth — sometimes with ham or sausage; often garnished with lime, sour cream, and cilantro.

name: Gingersnaps
notes: Crisp spiced cookies of molasses, butter, and ginger — rolled in sugar and baked until they crackle on top.

name: Beer bread
notes: A quick yeasted-tasting loaf of self-rising flour, sugar, and a bottle of beer — baked with melted butter on top for a crackly crust.

name: Texas sheet cake
notes: A thin chocolate-buttermilk sheet cake topped warm with a poured cocoa-pecan icing — sliced in squares from the pan.

name: Cream puffs
notes: A pâte à choux dough piped into mounds, baked into hollow shells, and filled with whipped cream or vanilla custard.

name: Harvard beets
notes: Sliced cooked beets glazed in a sweet-tart sauce of sugar, vinegar, and cornstarch with a knob of butter.

name: Stuffed green peppers
notes: Bell peppers blanched and filled with seasoned ground beef and rice in tomato sauce, baked until tender.

name: Death by chocolate
notes: A layered trifle of crumbled brownies, chocolate pudding (often spiked with Kahlúa), toffee bits, and whipped topping.

name: Wassail
notes: A hot holiday drink of apple cider, orange and lemon juice, and warm spices — slow-simmered; American versions are usually non-alcoholic.

name: Japanese fruit pie
notes: A Southern pie of eggs, sugar, and butter folded with coconut, raisins, and pecans baked in a single crust — Southern despite the name.

name: Broccoli rice casserole (variant)
notes: A cheesy-rice version with broccoli, cream of chicken or mushroom soup, and processed cheese — baked until bubbling.

name: Strawberry delight
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of shortbread crust, sweet cream cheese, strawberry pie filling, and whipped topping.

name: Peach pie
notes: A double-crust pie of sliced ripe peaches tossed with sugar and a thickener, baked until juices bubble and crust browns.

name: Cheese soup
notes: A creamy soup of diced vegetables and broth thickened with milk-and-roux and finished with Velveeta or processed cheese.

name: Cheese ball bites
notes: Mini cheese balls of cream cheese and shredded cheese rolled in chopped nuts or herbs — served as appetizers.

name: Parmesan-crusted chicken
notes: Chicken breasts coated in Parmesan, breadcrumbs, and herbs, then baked or pan-fried until golden — distinct from saucy chicken parmigiana.

name: Cheese biscuits
notes: A buttermilk biscuit dough mixed with sharp cheddar — sometimes brushed with garlic butter (Red Lobster style).

name: Chicken curry
notes: Chicken simmered in a spiced sauce — generic enough to span Indian, Thai, or Anglo-Indian preparations.

name: Sour cream coffee cake
notes: A tender Bundt or square cake enriched with sour cream and swirled with a cinnamon-sugar-pecan streusel.

name: Chicken soup
notes: Chicken simmered with carrots, celery, onion, and herbs in broth — the universal stockpot comfort food.

name: Wacky cake
notes: A Depression-era one-bowl chocolate cake with no eggs, milk, or butter — leavened with baking soda and vinegar, mixed right in the pan.

name: Coconut pound cake
notes: A dense pound cake folded with shredded coconut and coconut extract, often soaked with a coconut-rum or coconut-milk glaze.

name: Pralines
notes: A creamy New Orleans confection of pecans simmered in butter, sugar, cream, and vanilla, beaten and dropped to set.

name: Chicken tortilla soup
notes: A spiced tomato-chicken broth with shredded chicken, beans, and corn, ladled over crispy tortilla strips and topped with cheese, avocado, and lime.

name: Shrimp salad
notes: Cooked shrimp tossed with celery, hard-boiled egg, and a lemony mayo dressing — served chilled on greens or in a sandwich.

name: Minestrone soup
notes: A hearty Italian vegetable soup of beans, pasta, tomato, and seasonal vegetables in a herb-scented broth, finished with Parmesan.

name: Mandarin orange cake (pig pickin' cake)
notes: A yellow cake folded with canned mandarin oranges, topped with a whipped-cream-and-pineapple frosting — the Southern "pig pickin'" cake.

name: Candied sweet potatoes
notes: Sliced sweet potatoes baked in a butter-and-brown-sugar glaze with cinnamon — a Southern Thanksgiving side.

name: Zucchini pie
notes: A crustless quiche-style bake of sliced zucchini with eggs, mozzarella, Parmesan, and herbs.

name: Egg custard
notes: A baked or steamed custard of eggs, milk, sugar, and vanilla — silky and softly set, dusted with nutmeg.

name: Baked pineapple
notes: Crushed pineapple folded with eggs, sugar, and bread cubes, baked into a sweet-savory side served with ham.

name: Baked macaroni and cheese
notes: Elbow macaroni in a cheddar bechamel poured into a casserole, topped with more cheese and buttered breadcrumbs, baked until bubbly.

name: Lemon chicken
notes: Chicken breasts dredged and pan-fried, then finished in a lemon-butter pan sauce — sometimes thickened with flour.

name: Hamburger stroganoff
notes: Browned ground beef simmered with mushrooms and onion in a sour-cream-and-mushroom-soup gravy, served over egg noodles — a quick weeknight version of stroganoff.

name: Peanut butter bars
notes: A buttery peanut-butter shortbread base topped with a chocolate-peanut-butter frosting — cut into bars.

name: Pumpkin bars
notes: A sheet-pan version of pumpkin cake topped with cream cheese frosting, cut into squares.

name: Lemonade pie
notes: Frozen lemonade concentrate folded with sweetened condensed milk and whipped topping, poured into a graham crust and chilled until set.

name: Chicken supreme
notes: Chicken breasts simmered in a sour cream and cream-of-mushroom-soup sauce with onions and mushrooms — a 1950s casserole-style preparation.

name: Chocolate chess pie
notes: A Southern chess pie variant with cocoa or melted chocolate — a translucent, glossy chocolate custard in a flaky crust.

name: Blueberry pie
notes: A double-crust pie of fresh blueberries tossed with sugar and a thickener, baked until the filling bubbles through the lattice.

name: Twice baked potatoes
notes: Baked russet potatoes split, scooped, mashed with butter, sour cream, cheese, and bacon, returned to the shells, and baked again.

name: Chicken and broccoli casserole
notes: Cooked chicken and broccoli baked in a mayo, lemon juice, and cream-of-chicken-soup sauce, topped with cheese and buttered breadcrumbs.

name: Cornbread dressing
notes: Crumbled cornbread mixed with sauteed onions, celery, herbs, and broth, bound with eggs, and baked — the Southern Thanksgiving stuffing.

name: Texas hash
notes: Browned ground beef and rice simmered with onions, peppers, and chili-spiced tomato — then sometimes baked under cheese.

name: Butter cookies
notes: A simple piped or rolled shortbread of butter, sugar, flour, and vanilla — crisp and buttery.

name: Carrot casserole
notes: Sliced cooked carrots baked under a cheesy buttered-cracker topping — a Southern side dish.

name: Italian chicken
notes: Chicken pieces baked or simmered with Italian salad dressing or marinara — a low-effort weeknight preparation.

name: Butterscotch pie
notes: A baked pastry shell filled with brown-sugar-and-butter custard, topped with whipped cream or meringue.

name: Strawberry shortcake
notes: A split tender biscuit or sponge cake layered with macerated strawberries and whipped cream.

name: Strawberry pretzel salad (variant)
notes: Crushed-pretzel crust topped with sweetened cream cheese and strawberry-Jello-with-strawberries — chilled and cut into squares.

name: Lemon cake
notes: A bright lemon-scented butter or oil cake, often soaked or glazed with a tart lemon syrup or icing.

name: Baked spaghetti
notes: Cooked spaghetti layered with meat sauce and shredded mozzarella, then baked until the cheese browns and the edges crisp.

name: Bean dip
notes: Refried beans warmed with salsa and shredded cheese — sometimes layered with sour cream for chip-dipping.

name: Chocolate zucchini cake
notes: A moist cocoa cake folded with grated zucchini for tenderness — often a Bundt or sheet cake with chocolate chips on top.

name: Glazed carrots
notes: Sliced or baby carrots cooked in butter, brown sugar, and a splash of orange juice or stock until glossy.

name: Mexican chicken casserole
notes: Shredded chicken layered with tortilla chips, salsa or enchilada sauce, cream-of-chicken soup, and shredded cheese, baked until bubbly.

name: Pineapple cheese ball
notes: Cream cheese mixed with crushed pineapple, bell pepper, and onion, shaped into a ball and rolled in chopped pecans — served with crackers.

name: Split pea soup
notes: Dried split peas simmered with a ham hock or bone, carrots, onion, and celery until thick and creamy.

name: Pork chops
notes: Bone-in or boneless pork chops seasoned and pan-seared or baked — sometimes finished in a pan sauce.

name: Nacho dip
notes: Browned ground beef simmered with Velveeta and Rotel — a queso-style hot dip served with tortilla chips.

name: Coleslaw (variant)
notes: Shredded cabbage and carrot dressed in a sweet-tangy mayo or vinegar-based dressing — the picnic-staple side.

name: Rhubarb pie
notes: A double-crust or lattice pie of chopped rhubarb tossed with sugar and a thickener — tart and bright.

name: Custard pie
notes: A baked pastry shell filled with a sweet egg-milk-vanilla custard, dusted with nutmeg before baking.

name: Dumplings
notes: Soft drop-style dough of flour, milk, fat, and baking powder — dropped into simmering broth or stew to steam-cook.

name: 7-Up cake
notes: A lemon-lime pound cake made with a bottle of 7-Up soda — moist and citrus-bright.

name: Tomato soup
notes: Tomatoes simmered with onion, butter, and herbs, blended smooth and enriched with cream — often paired with grilled cheese.

name: Oatmeal pie
notes: A pecan-pie-style filling of eggs, sugar, butter, and oats — chewy and toasty in a single crust.

name: Apricot salad
notes: A molded gelatin salad of apricots and crushed pineapple set in orange Jello, often topped with a cream cheese layer.

name: Southern fried chicken
notes: Chicken pieces brined or buttermilk-soaked, dredged in seasoned flour, and deep-fried until crisp.

name: Jam cake
notes: A spiced Appalachian layer cake folded with blackberry or raspberry jam, often frosted with caramel icing.

name: Banana muffins
notes: Tender muffins of mashed banana, butter, sugar, and flour — a single-portion form of banana bread.

name: Rhubarb cake
notes: A tender butter or oil cake folded with chopped rhubarb, often topped with a brown-sugar streusel.

name: Chicken enchilada casserole
notes: A layered "stacked" enchilada bake of tortillas, shredded chicken, enchilada sauce, and cheese — assembled lasagna-style.

name: Cheeseburger pie
notes: Browned ground beef and onions baked under a Bisquick-and-egg crust with shredded cheese on top — a Bisquick-original "impossible" casserole.

name: Meatballs (variant)
notes: A ground beef meatball variant — bound with breadcrumbs, egg, milk, and seasonings, then browned and simmered in sauce.

name: Ground beef casserole
notes: Browned ground beef baked with potatoes or noodles, mushrooms, vegetables, and shredded cheese — a one-dish weeknight meal.

name: Forgotten cookies
notes: Beaten egg whites folded with sugar, mini chocolate chips, and chopped pecans — piped onto sheets and left in a turned-off oven overnight to dry.

name: Ambrosia
notes: A Southern fruit salad of mandarin oranges, pineapple, mini marshmallows, shredded coconut, and sour cream or whipped topping.

name: Chex party mix
notes: Chex cereals, pretzels, and mixed nuts coated in a buttery Worcestershire-and-seasoning blend, then baked or microwaved until crisp.

name: Vanilla wafer cake
notes: A butter-and-egg pound cake made with crushed vanilla wafers in place of flour, often folded with coconut and pecans.

name: Dirty rice
notes: White rice cooked with finely chopped chicken livers, gizzards, and ground meat, plus the trinity of vegetables and Cajun seasoning.

name: Hot rolls
notes: A soft enriched yeast dough proofed, shaped, and baked to be served warm with butter.

name: Eggplant parmesan
notes: Breaded eggplant slices fried, then baked in tomato sauce under layers of mozzarella and Parmesan — Italian-American comfort food.

name: Pumpkin muffins
notes: Spiced muffins of pumpkin puree, eggs, oil, and warm spices — often topped with streusel or chopped nuts.

name: Barbecue (pulled pork)
notes: Pulled or chopped slow-cooked pork shoulder dressed with a vinegar-or-tomato-based barbecue sauce — served on a soft bun.

name: Peanut butter candy
notes: A no-bake confection of peanut butter, sugar, butter, and milk cooked and beaten to a fudge — sometimes dipped in chocolate.

name: Green rice
notes: Rice baked with chopped broccoli or spinach, onion, cream of mushroom soup, and Cheez Whiz — a Southern church-supper side.

name: Lemon chess pie
notes: A Southern chess pie brightened with lemon juice and zest — translucent and tangy in a flaky crust.

name: Rice pilaf
notes: Long-grain rice toasted in butter with vermicelli or onions, then simmered in seasoned chicken broth.

name: Mexican rice
notes: Long-grain rice toasted in oil, then simmered with tomato sauce, garlic, and chicken broth until tender and orange-tinted.

name: Raw apple cake
notes: An oil-based spice cake folded with chopped raw apples and nuts — no need to precook the fruit.

name: Cowboy cookies
notes: Drop cookies of butter, brown sugar, oats, chocolate chips, and chopped pecans — a hearty oversized cookie.

name: Hot artichoke dip
notes: Chopped artichoke hearts baked with cream cheese, mayo, sour cream, and Parmesan until bubbling — served hot with bread or crackers.

name: Lime Jello salad
notes: Lime gelatin set with crushed pineapple, cottage cheese, whipped topping, and chopped pecans — a green Southern molded salad.

name: Magic cookie bars
notes: A graham crust topped with a glossy pour of sweetened condensed milk, then chocolate chips, coconut, and pecans — baked until set.

name: Veggie pizza (cold)
notes: A cold "pizza" of crescent-roll crust spread with herbed cream cheese and topped with chopped raw vegetables and shredded cheese.

name: Three bean salad (variant)
notes: Green, kidney, and wax beans tossed with onion and peppers in a sweet-tart vinegar dressing — chilled overnight.

name: Pineapple pie
notes: A pie of crushed pineapple set with eggs, sugar, and a touch of flour or lemon — sometimes topped with meringue.

name: Apple salad
notes: Diced apples tossed with pineapple, celery, and pecans in a sweet whipped-topping dressing — a Waldorf-style picnic salad.

name: Mandarin orange salad
notes: Mandarin oranges layered or molded with pineapple and orange gelatin — a chilled Southern fruit salad.

name: Homemade egg noodles
notes: A simple dough of flour, egg, milk, and salt rolled thin, cut into ribbons, and boiled in broth — served as a side or in soup.

name: Sticky buns
notes: Yeasted dough rolled with cinnamon-sugar, baked over a pan of brown-sugar-butter syrup with pecans, then inverted to serve.

name: Chess cake (ooey gooey butter cake)
notes: A yellow cake mix base topped with a cream-cheese-egg-and-powdered-sugar layer that bakes into a gooey "butter cake" — a St. Louis-Southern dessert.

name: Homemade peanut butter cups
notes: A peanut butter, powdered sugar, and graham-cracker filling sandwiched between layers of melted chocolate in muffin cups.

name: Stromboli
notes: Pizza dough rolled around layers of salami, ham, cheese, and peppers, sealed and baked into a sliced log.

name: Blondies
notes: Brown-sugar-and-butter bars in the shape of brownies but with vanilla in place of chocolate — sometimes with butterscotch or chocolate chips.

name: White chicken chili
notes: Shredded chicken simmered with white beans, green chiles, cumin, and broth — finished with sour cream or cream cheese.

name: Spaghetti with meat sauce
notes: Cooked spaghetti tossed with a long-simmered ground-beef-and-tomato sauce — the American weeknight pasta.

name: Chocolate chip pie
notes: A gooey pecan-pie-style filling of butter, sugar, eggs, and a touch of flour, packed with chocolate chips and walnuts — like a giant cookie in a pie shell.

name: Chicken marsala
notes: Pounded chicken cutlets dredged in flour, browned in butter, and finished in a Marsala-wine and mushroom pan sauce.

name: German chocolate cake
notes: A sweet-mild-chocolate layer cake filled and topped with a coconut-pecan caramel frosting — invented in Texas, named after German's baking chocolate.

name: Heavenly hash
notes: Crushed pineapple, mandarin oranges, mini marshmallows, and chopped pecans folded with whipped cream — a Southern dessert salad.

name: Stuffed shells
notes: Jumbo pasta shells filled with seasoned ricotta and spinach, nested in marinara, topped with mozzarella, and baked.

name: Southern pecan pie
notes: A custard of eggs, sugar, butter, and corn syrup or molasses studded with pecan halves, baked in a flaky crust until set.

name: Seven layer salad (variant)
notes: Lettuce, frozen peas, red onion, eggs, bacon, and cheese layered in a glass bowl, sealed under a mayo-and-sugar topping — chilled overnight.

name: Banana split pie
notes: A graham crust filled with sweet whipped cream cheese, sliced bananas, crushed pineapple, and whipped topping — banana-split flavors in pie form.

name: Chicken fajitas
notes: Marinated chicken strips seared with bell peppers and onions, served sizzling with warm tortillas and toppings.

name: Homemade Kahlúa
notes: A homemade coffee liqueur of strong brewed coffee, sugar, vanilla, and vodka — aged in a jar for a few weeks.

name: Mexican salad
notes: Lettuce tossed with seasoned ground beef, beans, cheese, tomatoes, and crushed tortilla chips with a creamy salsa dressing.

name: Cabbage soup
notes: Shredded cabbage simmered with ground beef, tomatoes, and other vegetables in a savory broth — sometimes the diet "cabbage soup".

name: Marinated mushrooms
notes: Whole button mushrooms tossed in a herb-and-vinegar marinade with oil, lemon, and seasonings — chilled as an appetizer.

name: Buttermilk pancakes
notes: A baking-soda-leavened buttermilk batter cooked in butter on a griddle — fluffy and tangy.

name: Mixed vegetable casserole
notes: A medley of mixed vegetables (often canned Veg-All) baked with mayo, onion, and shredded cheese under a buttered cracker top.

name: Lemon pound cake
notes: A dense pound cake brightened with lemon zest and juice, drizzled with a lemon-sugar glaze while still warm.

name: Banana cream pie
notes: A baked crust filled with vanilla pastry cream and sliced bananas, topped with whipped cream — chilled before serving.

name: Bean soup
notes: Dried beans simmered slowly with a ham hock or smoked meat, onion, celery, and broth until thick and rich.

name: Corned beef casserole
notes: Canned corned beef baked with egg noodles, cream of chicken or mushroom soup, peas, and Swiss cheese.

name: Stuffed bell peppers (variant)
notes: Bell peppers hollowed and filled with seasoned ground beef, rice, onion, and tomato sauce, baked until tender.

name: Turkey chili
notes: Ground turkey simmered with beans, tomatoes, peppers, and chili spices — a lighter take on classic chili.

name: Baked apples
notes: Whole cored apples stuffed with brown sugar, butter, raisins, and cinnamon, baked until tender — served warm with cream.

name: Cheesy potatoes (variant)
notes: Sliced or shredded potatoes baked with sour cream, shredded cheddar, and butter — the "funeral potatoes" comfort side.

name: Orange slice cake
notes: A dense buttermilk Bundt cake folded with chopped orange-slice candies, dates, coconut, and pecans, soaked with orange juice and sugar after baking.

name: Egg custard pie
notes: A baked pastry shell filled with a milk-egg-sugar custard, dusted with nutmeg — served chilled or barely warm.

name: Pineapple salad
notes: Crushed pineapple set with whipped topping, cream cheese, mini marshmallows, and pecans — a sweet Southern molded salad.

name: Oatmeal raisin cookies
notes: Drop cookies of butter, brown sugar, oats, raisins, and warm spices — chewy and homey.

name: Banana split dessert
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of graham crust, whipped butter-sugar-egg cream, sliced bananas, crushed pineapple, whipped topping, nuts, and cherries.

name: Marinated vegetables
notes: Mixed cooked or raw vegetables tossed in an oil-and-vinegar marinade with sugar and herbs — chilled overnight as a make-ahead salad.

name: Baked potato soup
notes: A creamy potato soup garnished like a loaded baked potato — sour cream, cheddar, bacon, and chives.

name: New England clam chowder (variant)
notes: Diced potatoes, salt pork or bacon, onions, and clams simmered in milk and cream — thick, creamy, and white.

name: Chocolate pecan pie
notes: A classic pecan-pie custard with melted chocolate or chocolate chips stirred in — fudgy beneath the toasted pecans.

name: Baked ziti
notes: Ziti tossed with marinara and ricotta, layered with mozzarella, and baked until the top blisters — Italian-American comfort food.

name: Congealed salad
notes: A molded gelatin salad of canned fruit, cream cheese, nuts, and whipped topping — a Southern potluck staple.

name: Barbecue chicken
notes: Bone-in chicken pieces grilled or baked and basted with a sweet-tangy barbecue sauce.

name: French coconut pie
notes: A custard of eggs, sugar, butter, vinegar, and vanilla folded with shredded coconut, baked into a single crust until golden.

name: Haystacks
notes: Melted butterscotch or chocolate stirred with chow mein noodles and peanuts, dropped onto wax paper to set into clustered "haystacks".

name: Vegetable beef soup
notes: Cubed or ground beef simmered with mixed vegetables, tomatoes, and herbs in beef broth — a stockpot weeknight soup.

name: Coconut macaroons
notes: Shredded coconut bound with egg whites and sweetened condensed milk, mounded onto sheets and baked until golden on top.

name: German chocolate upside-down cake
notes: A coconut-pecan layer on the bottom, batter on top, and a cream-cheese-and-powdered-sugar layer that swirls down through the cake — earthquake-cake style.

name: Cottage cheese salad
notes: Cottage cheese folded with crushed pineapple and mandarin oranges or other fruit — a high-protein chilled side.

name: Spoon bread
notes: A souffle-style cornmeal-milk-and-egg pudding baked until just set — soft enough to scoop with a spoon.

name: Spaghetti casserole
notes: Cooked spaghetti tossed with ground beef, mushrooms, and tomato sauce, then baked under shredded cheese.

name: Chicken wings
notes: Whole or split chicken wings baked or fried, then tossed in a sauce (Buffalo, honey-garlic, barbecue) — game-day finger food.

name: Cabbage salad
notes: Shredded cabbage tossed with a sweet vinaigrette and sometimes ramen noodles or almonds — a crunchy slaw variant.

name: Mayonnaise cake
notes: A Depression-era chocolate cake using mayonnaise in place of butter and eggs — the mayo carries the fat and emulsion.

name: Popovers
notes: A thin egg-milk-flour batter baked at high heat in hot buttered tins until they balloon into hollow rolls — close cousin of Yorkshire pudding.

name: Banana nut cake
notes: A banana butter cake with chopped walnuts or pecans folded in, often frosted with cream cheese icing.

name: Salmon croquettes
notes: Canned salmon mixed with egg, onion, and crackers or breadcrumbs, formed into patties and pan-fried until golden.

name: Better-than-sex cake
notes: A chocolate cake poked and drenched with sweetened condensed milk and caramel, topped with whipped topping and crushed toffee bits.

name: Lemon lush
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan-shortbread crust, sweetened cream cheese, lemon pudding, and whipped topping.

name: Zucchini cake
notes: An oil-based spice cake folded with grated zucchini, often frosted with cream cheese icing — a non-chocolate sibling of carrot cake.

name: Strawberry dessert
notes: Strawberry-and-pretzel or strawberry-and-cake-mix layered dessert with whipped cream — generic name for several Southern strawberry pan desserts.

name: Porcupine meatballs
notes: Ground beef and uncooked rice meatballs simmered in tomato sauce — the rice grains poke out as they cook, giving the "porcupine" look.

name: Cranberry bread
notes: A holiday quick bread of fresh or dried cranberries, orange zest, and walnuts in a tender batter.

name: Manicotti
notes: Pasta tubes filled with a ricotta-Parmesan-egg mixture, nested in marinara with mozzarella, and baked until bubbling.

name: Cake mix cookies
notes: A box of cake mix combined with eggs and oil to make a quick drop cookie — flavored with chocolate chips, sprinkles, or extracts.

name: Sauerkraut salad
notes: Drained sauerkraut tossed with chopped onion, bell pepper, and a sweet vinegar-and-oil dressing — chilled until tangy-sweet.

name: Beef burgundy
notes: Cubed beef braised slowly in Burgundy wine with mushrooms, onions, and herbs — the American-home version of boeuf bourguignon.

name: Piña colada cake
notes: A yellow cake poked and soaked with sweetened condensed milk and cream of coconut, topped with whipped topping and pineapple.

name: Baked pork chops
notes: Seasoned pork chops baked over rice, potatoes, or stuffing — sometimes covered in cream-of-mushroom soup or barbecue sauce.

name: Clam dip
notes: Cream cheese and sour cream whipped with minced clams, lemon, and Worcestershire — served chilled with chips or crackers.

name: Vegetarian chili
notes: A bean-and-vegetable chili of kidney, black, or pinto beans simmered with tomatoes, peppers, onions, and chili spices.

name: Buttermilk pound cake
notes: A dense, fine-crumb pound cake made tangy by buttermilk and lifted slightly by a touch of baking soda.

name: Sweet potato biscuits
notes: A biscuit dough enriched with mashed sweet potato — slightly sweet, orange-tinted, with a tender crumb.

name: Nachos
notes: Tortilla chips piled with seasoned ground beef, beans, melted cheese, jalapeños, salsa, sour cream, and guacamole.

name: Chicken rice casserole
notes: Raw rice and chicken pieces baked together in cream of mushroom soup and a packet of onion soup mix — a hands-off one-dish meal.

name: Millionaire pie
notes: A no-bake pie of sweetened condensed milk whipped with lemon juice and folded with crushed pineapple, pecans, and whipped topping — set in a graham crust.

name: Peanut clusters
notes: Roasted peanuts stirred into melted chocolate and dropped onto wax paper to set — a two-ingredient candy.

name: White bread
notes: A basic enriched yeasted loaf of bread flour, milk, sugar, butter, and yeast — soft and sandwich-friendly.

name: Scripture cake
notes: A spiced fruit-and-nut cake whose ingredients are named by their Bible references (Jeremiah's figs, Genesis's butter, etc.) — a Victorian church-supper novelty.

name: Orange Jello salad
notes: Orange gelatin set with mandarin oranges, crushed pineapple, and cottage cheese — sometimes layered with whipped topping.

name: Italian beef
notes: Thin-sliced beef slow-cooked in Italian-seasoned broth with giardiniera and bell peppers, piled on a long roll — the Chicago specialty.

name: Hawaiian chicken
notes: Chicken pieces baked or simmered in a sweet-tangy pineapple-and-soy or barbecue sauce, served over rice.

name: Chili dip
notes: Cream cheese spread in a dish, topped with canned chili and shredded cheese, then warmed until bubbly — a tailgate favorite.

name: Funnel cake
notes: A pancake-like batter drizzled in concentric circles into hot oil, fried crisp, and dusted heavily with powdered sugar — a fairground classic.

name: Blackberry cobbler
notes: Sweetened fresh blackberries baked under a tender biscuit or batter topping — served warm with ice cream.

name: Hungarian goulash
notes: Cubed beef slow-stewed with onions, peppers, and a generous amount of sweet paprika in a rich tomato-paprika gravy.

name: Rum cake
notes: A yellow-cake-mix Bundt with chopped pecans on the bottom, soaked after baking with a butter-sugar-rum syrup — Bacardi's classic.

name: Party potatoes
notes: Mashed potatoes whipped with cream cheese, sour cream, butter, and onion — a make-ahead potluck side baked until golden on top.

name: Icebox cookies
notes: A butter-sugar dough rolled into a log, chilled, then sliced and baked — yields uniform rounds of shortbread or spice cookie.

name: Applesauce
notes: Peeled apples simmered with sugar, cinnamon, and lemon until soft, then mashed smooth or chunky — eaten as a side or snack.

name: Stuffed cabbage
notes: Blanched cabbage leaves wrapped around seasoned ground beef and rice, then baked in tomato sauce — Eastern European golabki / golumpki.

name: Egg rolls
notes: Wheat wrappers rolled around stir-fried cabbage, pork, shrimp, and aromatics, then deep-fried golden — Chinese-American takeout style.

name: Gooey butter cake
notes: A yellow cake mix base topped with a cream-cheese-egg-and-powdered-sugar layer that bakes to a gooey, soft middle — St. Louis original.

name: Angel food cake
notes: A fat-free white sponge cake leavened only by whipped egg whites, baked in a tube pan and inverted to cool.

name: Caramel apple dip
notes: Cream cheese whipped with brown sugar, vanilla, and toffee bits — served with sliced apples for dipping.

name: Chocolate cream pie
notes: A baked pastry shell filled with a cooked chocolate pudding, topped with whipped cream and chocolate shavings.

name: Christmas punch
notes: A non-alcoholic holiday punch of cranberry juice, orange juice, pineapple juice, and ginger ale — served from a bowl over ice.

name: Blueberry cake
notes: A tender butter cake folded with fresh or frozen blueberries — sometimes a coffee-cake style with a crumb topping.

name: Persimmon pudding
notes: A dense baked pudding-cake of persimmon pulp, sugar, eggs, milk, and spices — a Midwestern autumn dessert.

name: Beef casserole
notes: Ground or cubed beef baked with rice or noodles, vegetables, mushrooms, and cheese — a one-dish weeknight bake.

name: Lemon bread
notes: A sweet quick bread bright with lemon zest and juice, finished with a tart lemon-sugar glaze.

name: Summer squash casserole
notes: Sliced yellow squash cooked tender, mixed with sour cream and cream of chicken soup, and baked under a buttery-cracker top.

name: Doughnuts
notes: A leavened or cake-style ring of dough deep-fried and finished with glaze, sugar, or cinnamon-sugar.

name: Raisin pie
notes: A double-crust pie of raisins simmered with sugar, lemon, and a touch of flour or cornstarch — "funeral pie" in Pennsylvania Dutch tradition.

name: Chicken and dressing casserole
notes: Cooked chicken layered with seasoned cornbread or stuffing dressing and bound with cream of mushroom soup — a Southern Thanksgiving-into-leftovers bake.

name: Broccoli cornbread
notes: A skillet cornbread enriched with chopped broccoli, cottage cheese, eggs, and butter — moist and savory.

name: Pumpkin pie cake (pumpkin dump cake)
notes: A pumpkin-pie custard layered under a yellow cake mix and pats of butter, baked into a self-streuseled hybrid dessert.

name: Chicken piccata
notes: Pounded chicken cutlets dredged in flour and pan-fried, finished in a lemon-and-white-wine pan sauce with capers and butter.

name: Toffee bars
notes: A brown-sugar-and-butter shortbread topped with melted chocolate and chopped nuts, cut into bars while still warm.

name: Pistachio cake
notes: A green-tinted Bundt cake from yellow-cake-mix and instant pistachio pudding, often made with club soda or 7-Up for tenderness.

name: Reuben casserole
notes: Layered corned beef, sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and rye breadcrumbs baked with Thousand Island dressing — Reuben sandwich flavors in casserole form.

name: Cherry dessert
notes: Cherry pie filling layered with sweetened cream cheese, a graham or pretzel crust, and whipped topping — a no-bake Southern dessert.

name: King Ranch chicken
notes: A Texas casserole of shredded chicken, tortilla strips, Rotel tomatoes-and-chiles, mushroom soup, and Velveeta — baked until creamy and bubbling.

name: Cheese wafers
notes: A short cheddar-and-butter dough piped or sliced from a log and baked into thin crisp savory rounds — cousin of cheese straws.

name: Cheese bread
notes: A quick bread or yeast loaf with shredded cheese baked into the dough and sometimes sprinkled on top.

name: Peanut butter blossoms
notes: Peanut butter cookies rolled in sugar and pressed with a Hershey's Kiss as soon as they come out of the oven.

name: Buttermilk salad
notes: Crushed pineapple cooked with orange Jello and folded into buttermilk and whipped topping — a tangy chilled Southern dessert salad.

name: Butterscotch brownies
notes: A brown-sugar-and-butter blondie packed with butterscotch chips and pecans — chewy and caramel-sweet.

name: Cocktail meatballs
notes: Small meatballs simmered in a sauce of grape jelly and chili sauce (or barbecue sauce) — held warm in a slow cooker for parties.

name: Five cup salad
notes: Equal cups of mandarin oranges, pineapple chunks, mini marshmallows, shredded coconut, and sour cream — chilled and stirred together.

name: Icebox fruitcake
notes: A no-bake fruitcake of crushed graham crackers or vanilla wafers mixed with candied fruit, dates, nuts, and sweetened condensed milk — pressed in a pan and chilled.

name: Turkey tetrazzini
notes: Cooked turkey baked with spaghetti or linguine, mushrooms, and a sherry-cream sauce under Parmesan and breadcrumbs — a Thanksgiving leftover staple.

name: Lemon icebox pie
notes: A no-bake pie of lemon juice whisked into sweetened condensed milk and egg yolks, chilled in a graham crust — set by acid, not baking.

name: Caramel pie
notes: A pie of brown-sugar-and-milk caramel pudding poured into a baked crust, topped with whipped cream — sometimes made with boiled sweetened condensed milk.

name: Hominy casserole
notes: Canned hominy baked with cheese, green chiles, and sour cream until bubbly — a Southwestern side.

name: Seafood casserole
notes: Shrimp, crab, or scallops baked with rice or cracker crumbs in a cream-or-mushroom-soup sauce, topped with cheese or buttered crumbs.

name: Fruitcake cookies
notes: Drop cookies of candied fruit, dates, raisins, and pecans bound by a buttermilk-and-bourbon-style spiced batter — fruitcake flavor in a cookie.

name: Pico de gallo
notes: Diced tomato, white onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime — a fresh, chunky Mexican salsa served as a dip or topping.

name: Christmas cookies
notes: A category-name for spiced and decorated rolled or drop cookies baked for the holidays — typically sugar, gingerbread, or fruit-and-nut.

name: Broccoli bread
notes: A savory cornbread enriched with chopped broccoli, cottage cheese, butter, and eggs — baked in a skillet or pan.

name: Cheesy baked potatoes
notes: Sliced or cubed potatoes baked with butter, sour cream, cheese, and onions — generic "potatoes" usually means the funeral-potatoes side.

name: Orange balls
notes: Crushed vanilla wafers mixed with butter, frozen orange juice concentrate, and powdered sugar, rolled into balls and coated with coconut.

name: Chocolate ice cream
notes: A churned custard of cocoa or melted chocolate, milk, cream, sugar, and egg yolks — the chocolate baseline.

name: Tortilla roll-ups
notes: Flour tortillas spread with seasoned cream cheese, salsa, olives, and green chiles, rolled and sliced into pinwheels.

name: Fettuccine alfredo
notes: Fresh fettuccine tossed with butter and grated Parmesan until emulsified into a creamy sauce — American versions add heavy cream.

name: Buffalo chicken dip
notes: Shredded chicken baked with cream cheese, ranch or blue cheese dressing, and Buffalo wing sauce, topped with shredded cheese.

name: German chocolate pie
notes: A baked chocolate-and-evaporated-milk custard topped with the classic coconut-pecan caramel — German chocolate cake flavors in a pie.

name: Stuffed zucchini
notes: Zucchini halved lengthwise, hollowed, and filled with seasoned ground beef or sausage, breadcrumbs, and cheese, then baked.

name: Spinach quiche
notes: A butter pastry shell filled with an egg-and-cream custard, sautéed spinach, and Swiss or feta — a meatless quiche variant.

name: Chocolate pudding
notes: Cocoa, sugar, milk, and cornstarch cooked into a thick pudding with butter and vanilla — chilled with plastic wrap pressed on the surface.

name: Broccoli and cauliflower salad
notes: Raw broccoli and cauliflower florets tossed with bacon, red onion, and a sweet mayonnaise dressing — broccoli-salad style.

name: Sausage cheese balls
notes: Bite-size baked balls of breakfast sausage, shredded cheddar, and biscuit mix — the same Southern appetizer as sausage balls.

name: Banana punch
notes: Mashed bananas blended with frozen juice concentrates and sugar, frozen, then thinned with ginger ale at serving — a slushy non-alcoholic party punch.

name: Hot cocoa mix
notes: A pantry mix of powdered milk, cocoa, sugar, and powdered creamer — stirred into hot water for instant cocoa.

name: Beef stew
notes: Cubed beef braised slowly with potatoes, carrots, onions, and seasonings in beef broth until thick and tender.

name: Cherry cobbler
notes: Sweet-tart cherries baked under a tender biscuit or batter topping — served warm with cream or ice cream.

name: Guacamole dip
notes: Mashed avocados seasoned with lime, salt, onion, jalapeño, and cilantro — eaten with tortilla chips.

name: Strawberry pizza
notes: A sugar-cookie crust spread with sweetened cream cheese and topped with sliced fresh strawberries and a strawberry glaze.

name: Oyster stew
notes: Shucked oysters and their liquor simmered briefly in butter, milk, and cream with celery and onions — a New England Christmas tradition.

name: Apple fritters
notes: Chopped apples folded into a leavened batter, dropped into hot oil, fried golden, and finished with cinnamon-sugar or a glaze.

name: Chicken and dressing
notes: Shredded cooked chicken served alongside or layered with seasoned cornbread or bread dressing — Thanksgiving plate, Southern style.

name: Blueberry cobbler
notes: Sweetened fresh or frozen blueberries baked under a buttery biscuit or cake topping — served warm with ice cream.

name: Marinated vegetable salad
notes: Cooked or raw mixed vegetables tossed in an oil-and-vinegar dressing with sugar and herbs — chilled overnight as a make-ahead side.

name: Ginger cookies
notes: Soft or crisp spiced cookies of butter, molasses, brown sugar, ground ginger, and warm spices — rolled in sugar before baking.

name: Ice cream cake
notes: Layers of ice cream pressed into a cake pan with a cookie or crumb base, frozen solid, then frosted with whipped cream.

name: Sweet potato pudding
notes: Grated raw or mashed cooked sweet potato baked with eggs, milk, sugar, butter, and warm spices into a soft custard-cake.

name: Minestrone
notes: A thick Italian vegetable soup of beans, pasta, and seasonal vegetables in a tomato-and-Parmesan-rind broth.

name: Raisin bran muffins
notes: High-fiber muffins of wheat bran or bran cereal, raisins, buttermilk, and a touch of molasses — moist and lightly sweet.

name: Mashed potato casserole
notes: Mashed potatoes whipped with cream cheese, sour cream, butter, and seasonings, baked under shredded cheese — make-ahead party potatoes.

name: Corn dogs
notes: Hot dogs on a stick dipped in a sweetened cornmeal batter and deep-fried golden — a fairground staple.

name: Apple cobbler
notes: Spiced sliced apples baked under a tender biscuit or batter topping — a homier cousin of apple pie.

name: Texas caviar
notes: Black-eyed peas marinated with diced peppers, onions, and tomatoes in Italian dressing — served cold with tortilla chips.

name: Coca-Cola cake
notes: A buttermilk-and-cocoa sheet cake with a bottle of Coca-Cola stirred into the batter, finished with a warm cola-pecan icing.

name: Cherry crunch
notes: Cherry pie filling baked under a yellow-cake-mix-and-butter streusel with chopped pecans — sometimes called cherry dump cake.

name: Date nut bread
notes: A spiced quick bread folded with chopped dates and walnuts — moist, lightly sweet, often served with cream cheese.

name: Hot German potato salad
notes: Sliced warm potatoes dressed with a tangy bacon-fat-and-vinegar dressing, served hot — the classic German preparation.

name: Spiced pecans
notes: Pecan halves coated in an egg-white-and-sugar slurry with cinnamon and cayenne, baked slowly until crisp.

name: Orange cake
notes: A bright butter or oil cake scented with orange zest and juice, often soaked or glazed with an orange-sugar syrup.

name: Sand tarts (pecan snowballs)
