notes: A butter-and-powdered-sugar shortbread cookie folded with finely chopped pecans, baked, and rolled in more powdered sugar.

name: Shrimp mold
notes: A chilled appetizer mold of cream cheese, mayonnaise, gelatin, and chopped shrimp — turned out and served with crackers.

name: Shrimp casserole
notes: Shrimp baked with rice or noodles, peppers and onions, and a creamy mushroom-soup sauce — topped with cheese and crumbs.

name: Date balls
notes: Chopped dates cooked with butter, sugar, and egg, then stirred with Rice Krispies and pecans, rolled into balls and dusted in powdered sugar or coconut.

name: Chicken à la king
notes: Diced cooked chicken in a cream sauce with mushrooms, pimientos, and sherry — served over toast points or rice.

name: Cheese puffs
notes: A pâte à choux dough enriched with grated cheese, piped or dropped into mounds and baked into airy savory bites (gougères).

name: Lemonade
notes: Fresh-squeezed lemon juice with sugar and water — served cold over ice.

name: Scones
notes: A short, dense quick bread of flour, cold butter, sugar, and milk or cream — wedge-cut and baked, often with currants or berries.

name: Fantasy fudge
notes: A microwave or stovetop fudge of sugar, butter, evaporated milk, chocolate chips, marshmallow creme, and walnuts — Kraft's classic recipe.

name: White chicken chili (variant)
notes: Shredded chicken simmered with white beans, green chiles, cumin, and broth, finished with sour cream or cream cheese.

name: 24-hour salad
notes: A layered icebox salad of lettuce, peas, eggs, bacon, cheese, and onion sealed under a mayo-and-sugar topping, chilled overnight (24 hours).

name: Crêpes
notes: Thin pancakes of flour, eggs, and milk cooked in a buttered pan and filled or rolled with sweet or savory fillings.

name: Eclair cake
notes: A no-bake icebox cake of graham crackers layered with vanilla pudding, topped with chocolate frosting — softens to eclair-like texture overnight.

name: Chicken stew
notes: Chicken pieces simmered with potatoes, carrots, onions, and herbs in seasoned broth until tender — homier than gumbo.

name: Shrimp spread
notes: Cream cheese whipped with chopped shrimp, lemon, Worcestershire, and seasonings — served chilled with crackers.

name: Popcorn cake
notes: Popped corn, gumdrops, and peanuts pressed into a Bundt pan with a hot marshmallow-and-butter syrup, set, and inverted to slice.

name: Oatmeal muffins
notes: Tender muffins of soaked oats, flour, brown sugar, eggs, and milk — sometimes with raisins or chopped nuts.

name: Chinese chicken salad
notes: Shredded cabbage and lettuce tossed with chicken, crushed ramen noodles or wonton strips, sesame seeds, almonds, and a soy-vinegar dressing.

name: Sourdough bread
notes: A bread leavened by a wild-yeast starter rather than commercial yeast — tangy, chewy, with a deeply browned crust.

name: Seafood gumbo
notes: A Louisiana stew of shrimp, crab, and sometimes oysters in a dark-roux broth with the trinity of vegetables, okra, and Creole spices — served over rice.

name: Barbecued chicken
notes: Bone-in chicken grilled or baked, basted repeatedly with barbecue sauce as it cooks until glazed and sticky.

name: Hot potato salad
notes: Boiled potatoes tossed warm with bacon, onion, sugar, and a vinegar dressing — the German-American hot variant.

name: Spinach lasagna
notes: Layered pasta sheets with ricotta, chopped spinach, mozzarella, and marinara — the meatless version of lasagna.

name: English toffee
notes: Butter and sugar cooked to hard-crack stage, poured onto a sheet, topped with melted chocolate and chopped almonds, then broken into shards.

name: Caramels
notes: Cream, butter, sugar, and corn syrup cooked slowly to firm-ball stage, poured to set, and cut into chewy squares.

name: Bean casserole (calico)
notes: A mix of canned baked, kidney, and butter beans baked with ground beef, bacon, brown sugar, and barbecue sauce — also called calico beans.

name: Cherry pie
notes: A double-crust or lattice pie of pitted sweet or sour cherries tossed with sugar and a thickener.

name: Onion soup
notes: Slowly caramelized onions simmered in beef broth with wine and herbs, ladled over toast and broiled under a cap of melted cheese.

name: Honey bun cake
notes: A yellow cake mix batter with sour cream baked with a swirl of cinnamon-brown-sugar, finished with a powdered-sugar-and-vanilla glaze — tastes like a honey bun.

name: Egg casserole
notes: A breakfast bake of beaten eggs, milk, cheese, bread, and breakfast sausage or ham — assembled the night before and baked in the morning.

name: Spoon rolls
notes: A yeasted batter dropped by the spoonful into muffin tins and baked — no kneading, no shaping, soft and roll-like.

name: Slaw
notes: Shredded cabbage and carrot dressed with mayo or vinegar — the generic short-name for coleslaw.

name: Au gratin potatoes
notes: Sliced potatoes layered with onions and Gruyère or cheddar in a milk-and-cream sauce, baked until bubbling with a golden cheese crust.

name: Fudge brownies
notes: Dense, rich brownies leaning fudgy rather than cakey — high butter and cocoa, low flour, baked just until the center sets.

name: Cream cheese cookies
notes: A butter-and-cream-cheese shortbread piped or cut into delicate cookies — tender and slightly tangy.

name: Butternut squash soup
notes: Roasted butternut squash simmered with onion, apple, and broth, blended smooth and finished with cream and warm spices.

name: Swedish meatballs
notes: Small, allspice-and-nutmeg-spiced meatballs of beef and pork, pan-fried and finished in a creamy beef-stock gravy.

name: Strawberry Jello salad
notes: Strawberry gelatin set with frozen strawberries and crushed pineapple, layered with sour cream — a chilled Southern dessert salad.

name: Sausage bread
notes: Frozen bread dough rolled around cooked Italian sausage, mozzarella, and peppers, then baked into a sliceable savory loaf.

name: Snowball cookies
notes: A butter-and-powdered-sugar shortbread folded with finely chopped pecans, baked into balls, and rolled in powdered sugar — also called Russian tea cakes.

name: Wild rice casserole
notes: Wild and long-grain rice baked with mushrooms, onions, and broth — often with chicken or sausage stirred in.

name: Party cheese ball
notes: Cream cheese mixed with shredded cheddar, Worcestershire, garlic, and seasonings, shaped into a ball and rolled in chopped pecans or parsley.

name: Taffy apple salad
notes: Diced apples, crushed pineapple, and peanuts folded with a cooked egg-and-flour dressing (mimicking caramel apple coating) — chilled overnight.

name: Boiled cookies (no-bake)
notes: Cocoa, butter, sugar, and milk boiled to a fudge, then stirred with oats and peanut butter and dropped to set — same family as no-bake cookies.

name: Summer salad
notes: A loose name for a mixed salad of fresh-from-the-garden tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, onions, and herbs in an oil-and-vinegar dressing.

name: Chocolate cookies
notes: Drop cookies of cocoa or melted chocolate in a butter-sugar dough — sometimes with chips, sometimes plain.

name: Soft pretzels
notes: A yeasted dough dipped briefly in a baking-soda water bath, shaped into pretzels, salted, and baked until deep brown — chewy and shiny.

name: Crab salad
notes: Lump or imitation crab tossed with celery, onion, and a lemony mayo dressing — served chilled on greens or as a sandwich filling.

name: Pizza burgers
notes: Ground beef simmered with pizza sauce and pepperoni, spooned on toasted English muffins or buns, and topped with mozzarella — broiled until bubbly.

name: Crazy cake (Wacky cake variant)
notes: A one-bowl Depression-era chocolate cake with no eggs, butter, or milk — leavened by vinegar reacting with baking soda; mixed right in the pan.

name: Yellow squash casserole
notes: Sliced yellow squash baked with eggs, sour cream, and cheese under a buttered cracker topping — a Southern church-supper side.

name: 7-Up salad
notes: Lemon-lime Jello set with crushed pineapple, mandarin oranges, and a bottle of 7-Up, sometimes folded with cream cheese topping.

name: Seafood salad
notes: Cooked shrimp, crab, or imitation crab tossed with celery, onion, and a lemon-mayo dressing — served chilled on greens or in sandwiches.

name: Ranger cookies
notes: A chewy drop cookie with oats, coconut, cornflakes (or Rice Krispies), and brown sugar — sometimes with chocolate chips or raisins.

name: Granola bars
notes: Oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruit bound by a honey-and-butter syrup, pressed into a pan and baked or chilled until set.

name: Pizza dip
notes: Cream cheese spread topped with marinara, mozzarella, and pepperoni, baked until melty — served with breadsticks or chips.

name: Mashed sweet potatoes
notes: Boiled or baked sweet potatoes mashed with butter, brown sugar, eggs, and warm spices — sometimes baked under marshmallows or streusel.

name: Stroganoff
notes: Strips of beef sautéed with mushrooms and onion in a sour-cream-and-mustard sauce — served over noodles or rice.

name: Chop suey
notes: A Chinese-American stir-fry of beef or chicken with celery, bean sprouts, onions, and mushrooms in a soy-thickened sauce, served over rice or noodles.

name: Baklava
notes: Layers of buttered phyllo and chopped nuts baked until crisp, then soaked in a honey-and-citrus syrup — a Levantine and Eastern-Mediterranean pastry.

name: Christmas salad
notes: A holiday Jello mold or fruit salad of cranberries, oranges, pineapple, and pecans set with red or green gelatin and cream cheese.

name: Creamed spinach
notes: Chopped spinach folded into a nutmeg-scented bechamel and finished with grated Parmesan — a steakhouse classic.

name: Rhubarb custard pie
notes: Chopped rhubarb set in a sweet eggs-and-cream custard, baked in a single crust — tangy filling against a tender custard.

name: Oatmeal chocolate chip cookies
notes: Drop cookies of oats, butter, brown sugar, and chocolate chips — chewier than chocolate chip cookies thanks to the oats.

name: Pumpkin soup
notes: Pumpkin puree simmered with onion, chicken stock, and warm spices, blended smooth and finished with cream.

name: Fresh peach pie
notes: Sliced fresh peaches arranged in a pre-baked crust and set with a cooked sugar-and-cornstarch glaze — chilled rather than baked.

name: Candied yams
notes: Sliced sweet potatoes baked in a butter-and-brown-sugar syrup with cinnamon and nutmeg — sometimes finished with marshmallows.

name: Jalapeño cornbread
notes: A skillet cornbread enriched with cheddar, creamed corn, and chopped jalapeños — moist and lightly spicy.

name: Potato candy
notes: Mashed potato kneaded with powdered sugar into a pliable dough, rolled around peanut butter, and sliced into pinwheels.

name: Bruschetta
notes: Toasted slices of crusty bread rubbed with garlic and topped with diced tomatoes, basil, and olive oil.

name: Coconut custard pie
notes: A baked egg-milk-sugar custard with shredded coconut, set in a single pastry shell — the cooked version of a coconut cream pie.

name: Apple crunch
notes: Spiced sliced apples baked under a brown-sugar-flour-butter streusel — a simpler cousin of apple crisp without oats.

name: Rum balls
notes: Crushed vanilla wafers or graham crackers mixed with cocoa, powdered sugar, corn syrup, pecans, and a slug of rum — rolled into balls and dusted in sugar.

name: Chicken delight
notes: A casserole or skillet of chicken breasts simmered with cream of mushroom soup, white wine or sherry, and mushrooms over rice or noodles.

name: Barbecued spareribs
notes: Pork spareribs slow-roasted or grilled with a sweet-tangy barbecue sauce until the meat pulls cleanly from the bone.

name: Strawberry punch
notes: Strawberries blended with pineapple juice, lemonade, and ginger ale — a pink non-alcoholic party drink.

name: Rice salad
notes: Cooked white rice tossed with chopped vegetables, olives, and an oil-and-vinegar dressing — served chilled as a picnic side.

name: Sour cream cookies
notes: Soft, cakey drop cookies enriched with sour cream and a hint of nutmeg — sometimes topped with a powdered-sugar glaze.

name: Jewish apple cake
notes: A dairy-free tube-pan cake of oil, eggs, orange juice, and cinnamon-sugar-tossed apples layered into the batter — a Pennsylvania-Jewish standard.

name: Scalloped pineapple
notes: Crushed pineapple folded with eggs, sugar, butter, and bread cubes, baked into a sweet-savory side served alongside ham.

name: Macaroni casserole
notes: Cooked macaroni baked with cheese, vegetables, and a creamy soup-based sauce — sometimes with ground beef stirred in.

name: Sour cream cake
notes: A tender Bundt or pound cake enriched with sour cream — sometimes swirled with cinnamon-pecan streusel.

name: Onion rings
notes: Sliced onion rings dipped in a milk-and-egg batter or breaded, then deep-fried until crisp and golden.

name: Eggnog
notes: Beaten eggs whipped with sugar, milk, cream, and spiced spirits (bourbon, rum, or brandy), topped with nutmeg — a holiday drink.

name: Crumb cake
notes: A tender butter cake topped with a thick brown-sugar-cinnamon-and-butter streusel — New York coffee-shop style.

name: Congo squares
notes: A brown-sugar-butter blondie packed with chocolate chips and chopped pecans, baked in a sheet pan and cut into squares.

name: Milky Way cake
notes: A chocolate-caramel butter cake made by melting Milky Way candy bars into the batter, often frosted with a chocolate-marshmallow icing.

name: Oatmeal bread
notes: A soft yeasted sandwich loaf with rolled oats soaked in hot water and worked into the dough — hearty and slightly sweet.

name: Cornbread salad
notes: Crumbled cornbread layered with beans, tomatoes, bacon, cheese, and ranch dressing in a glass bowl — a Southern potluck dish.

name: Vegetable lasagna
notes: Layered pasta sheets with ricotta, sautéed mixed vegetables (zucchini, spinach, mushrooms), mozzarella, and marinara — the meatless lasagna.

name: Crawfish étouffée
notes: Crawfish tails simmered in a blond roux with the holy trinity of vegetables and Creole seasoning, served over rice.

name: Frozen cranberry salad
notes: Cranberry sauce folded with crushed pineapple, cream cheese, whipped cream, and pecans, frozen in a pan and sliced — a holiday side-as-dessert.

name: Green bean salad
notes: Cooked green beans tossed with peppers, onions, and a sweet-tart vinegar dressing — chilled overnight.

name: Pink salad
notes: A pink Jello-and-cream-cheese mold set with crushed pineapple, maraschino cherries, and chopped pecans — a Southern church-cookbook dessert.

name: Zucchini soup
notes: Sliced zucchini simmered with onion, herbs, and chicken broth, blended smooth and finished with cream or yogurt.

name: Pineapple cookies
notes: A soft drop cookie made with crushed pineapple folded into a butter-sugar-egg batter, sometimes glazed.

name: Pumpkin cheesecake
notes: A baked cheesecake of cream cheese, pumpkin puree, and warm spices on a graham-cracker or pecan crust — a Thanksgiving alternative to pumpkin pie.

name: Peach crisp
notes: Sweetened sliced peaches baked under a crunchy oat-and-butter streusel — served warm, often with ice cream.

name: Beef jerky
notes: Strips of lean beef marinated in soy, Worcestershire, and spices, then slowly dried in a low oven or dehydrator until chewy.

name: Chocolate truffles
notes: Chocolate ganache (chocolate and warm cream) chilled, scooped into balls, and rolled in cocoa, nuts, or coatings.

name: Oven beef stew
notes: Cubed beef and root vegetables tossed with tomato juice or soup and seasonings, sealed in a Dutch oven, and baked low for hours.

name: Five cup salad (variant)
notes: Equal cups of mandarin oranges, pineapple chunks, mini marshmallows, shredded coconut, and sour cream — same Southern dessert as five-cup salad.

name: Caramel brownies
notes: A chocolate-cake-mix batter with a layer of melted caramel-and-evaporated-milk filling and chocolate chips, baked into bars.

name: Cherry cheese pie
notes: A no-bake pie of sweetened cream cheese filling in a graham crust, topped with canned cherry pie filling.

name: Pork chops and rice
notes: Bone-in pork chops baked over raw rice and broth (or cream of mushroom soup) until both are tender.

name: Barbecue beef
notes: Slow-cooked shredded beef (chuck or brisket) tossed in a sweet-tangy barbecue sauce, served on buns or over rice.

name: Spinach pie
notes: Chopped spinach baked in a pastry crust or phyllo with eggs, feta, and herbs — a quiche-or-spanakopita-style bake.

name: Ham rolls
notes: Slices of ham spread with cream cheese, rolled around a pickle spear or asparagus, and sliced into pinwheels — a cocktail appetizer.

name: Chicken noodle casserole
notes: Cooked egg noodles baked with shredded chicken, peas, and cream of mushroom or chicken soup under a cheese-and-crumb topping.

name: Egg drop soup
notes: Chicken broth thickened with cornstarch, into which beaten egg is streamed to form delicate ribbons — a Chinese-American restaurant staple.

name: Carrot bread
notes: A spiced quick bread folded with grated carrots — moist and lightly sweet, often with raisins or nuts.

name: Date bars
notes: Cooked dates sandwiched between layers of an oat-and-brown-sugar crumble, baked and cut into bars.

name: Broccoli bake
notes: Broccoli florets baked in a cheese-and-cream-of-mushroom-soup sauce with mushrooms and an egg-bound topping.

name: Baked chicken breasts
notes: Boneless chicken breasts baked with sour cream and cream of mushroom soup until tender — a low-effort weeknight bake.

name: Broccoli cheese casserole
notes: Broccoli florets baked with rice, cream of mushroom soup, and Cheez Whiz or shredded cheddar — a Southern potluck side.

name: Wedding punch
notes: A non-alcoholic punch of mixed juices and ginger ale or sherbet — served from a bowl at receptions.

name: Brunch casserole
notes: A make-ahead bake of eggs, milk, cheese, bread, and ham or sausage — assembled overnight and baked in the morning.

name: Plum cake
notes: A spiced oil-based cake folded with chopped fresh plums or strained baby-food plums — moist and lightly fruity.

name: Holiday punch
notes: A festive non-alcoholic punch of cranberry, orange, and pineapple juices with ginger ale — served from a bowl with citrus floats.

name: Tomato pie
notes: Sliced ripe tomatoes layered in a baked pie crust with basil, then topped with a mixture of mayo and shredded cheese, baked until golden.

name: Chicken nuggets
notes: Bite-size pieces of chicken breast breaded or battered and baked or fried — a kid-friendly favorite.

name: Cavatini
notes: A baked pasta casserole of ziti, rotini, or shells with ground beef, Italian sausage, peppers, marinara, and mozzarella — Pizza Hut-style.

name: Chili con queso
notes: Velveeta-style processed cheese melted with chiles, tomatoes, and aromatics — served warm with tortilla chips.

name: Hello dollies (seven-layer bars)
notes: A graham-cracker crust topped with butterscotch chips, chocolate chips, shredded coconut, and chopped pecans, drizzled with sweetened condensed milk and baked.

name: Cashew chicken
notes: Diced chicken stir-fried with cashews, peppers, and onions in a soy-and-ginger sauce — served over rice.

name: Jello poke cake
notes: A baked white or yellow cake poked all over and saturated with fruit-flavored gelatin, then topped with whipped topping — a 1970s potluck classic.

name: Ham casserole
notes: Cubed ham baked with potatoes or noodles, peas, and cheese in a cream-of-mushroom or cheese sauce — a leftover-ham one-dish meal.

name: Congo bars
notes: Brown-sugar-and-butter blondies packed with chocolate chips and chopped nuts — chewy and toffee-flavored.

name: Shortbread
notes: A classic Scottish biscuit of just butter, sugar, and flour — pressed flat or pricked, baked low, and cut into wedges or fingers.

name: Orange chicken
notes: Battered chicken pieces deep-fried and tossed in a glossy orange-and-soy glaze — the Panda Express American-Chinese standard.

name: Breakfast burritos
notes: Flour tortillas wrapped around scrambled eggs, breakfast sausage or bacon, cheese, and potatoes — sometimes salsa and beans too.

name: M&M cookies
notes: Classic drop cookies with M&M candies pressed into a butter-brown-sugar dough — bright and chewy.

name: Chicken and noodles
notes: Shredded chicken simmered with thick egg noodles in chicken broth — served over mashed potatoes in Midwestern style.

name: Italian meatballs
notes: Ground beef and pork mixed with breadcrumbs, egg, milk, Parmesan, and herbs, rolled into balls and simmered in marinara.

name: Squash pie
notes: A custard pie of pureed winter squash or butternut, eggs, milk, sugar, and warm spices — close cousin of pumpkin pie.

name: French bread
notes: A long, crusty yeasted loaf of flour, water, salt, and yeast — light interior, crackly crust.

name: Baking powder biscuits
notes: A quick bread of flour, baking powder, milk, and cold fat — patted, cut, and baked into tender flaky rounds.

name: Blueberry delight
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan shortbread crust, sweetened cream cheese, blueberry pie filling, and whipped topping.

name: Brisket
notes: A tough cut of beef seasoned and slowly cooked low (smoked, braised, or oven-roasted) until fork-tender.

name: Scalloped oysters
notes: Shucked oysters layered with crushed crackers, butter, and seasonings, soaked in milk or cream and baked until just set.

name: Pecan pralines
notes: Sugar, cream, butter, and pecans cooked to soft-ball, beaten, and dropped onto wax paper to set — the New Orleans candy.

name: Zucchini quiche
notes: Sliced zucchini baked in an egg-and-cheese custard, sometimes in a Bisquick-based crustless form.

name: Chili cheese dip
notes: Cream cheese spread in a dish, topped with canned chili and shredded cheese, baked or microwaved until bubbly.

name: Tomato soup cake
notes: A Depression-era spice cake leavened by a can of condensed tomato soup in place of milk — moist with raisins or nuts.

name: Devil's food cake
notes: A dark, tender chocolate layer cake leavened with baking soda — moister and richer than standard chocolate cake.

name: Cranberry chicken
notes: Chicken pieces baked over a sauce of jellied cranberry sauce and Catalina or French dressing mixed with onion soup mix.

name: Spiced nuts
notes: Mixed nuts coated in an egg-white-and-sugar slurry with cinnamon, ginger, and cayenne, baked slowly until crisp.

name: Chicken chili
notes: Shredded or ground chicken simmered with beans, peppers, tomatoes, and chili spices — a lighter alternative to beef chili.

name: Cold oven pound cake
notes: A dense pound cake placed in a cold oven and slow-baked as the oven heats up — gives a thick crisp crust and tender crumb.

name: Apricot nectar cake
notes: A yellow Bundt cake made with apricot nectar and lemon-flavored gelatin, soaked after baking with a lemon-sugar glaze.

name: Lemon curd
notes: Lemon juice, sugar, eggs, and butter cooked gently until thickened to a glossy spreadable curd — used on scones, cakes, or by the spoon.

name: Oriental ramen salad
notes: Shredded cabbage and lettuce tossed with crushed ramen noodles, slivered almonds, sesame seeds, and a soy-vinegar dressing.

name: Vidalia onion casserole
notes: Sliced sweet Vidalia onions baked with butter, cream, eggs, and shredded cheese under a buttered cracker crust — a Georgia favorite.

name: Stuffed pork chops
notes: Thick-cut pork chops cut with a pocket and filled with herbed bread stuffing, then baked or seared.

name: Whoopie pies
notes: Two cake-like chocolate cookies sandwiched around a fluffy marshmallow or vanilla buttercream filling — Pennsylvania Dutch and New England favorite.

name: Italian pasta salad
notes: Cooked rotini or penne tossed with peppers, olives, pepperoni, mozzarella, and Italian dressing — a picnic staple.

name: Creamy rice pudding
notes: Cooked rice simmered slowly in milk with sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon until thick and creamy — served warm or chilled.

name: Crab casserole
notes: Lump crab mixed with mayonnaise, eggs, milk, peppers, and breadcrumbs, baked under buttered cracker crumbs and cheese.

name: Homemade summer sausage
notes: Ground beef mixed with cure (Morton Tender Quick), seasonings, and liquid smoke, shaped into logs and baked slowly — a homemade cured sausage.

name: Pecan pie bars
notes: A shortbread crust topped with pecan-pie custard, baked and cut into bars — pecan pie in finger-food form.

name: Corn soufflé
notes: A puffed-up bake of corn kernels, cream-style corn, eggs, butter, sour cream, and a touch of cornbread mix — pudding-like and slightly sweet.

name: Southern green beans
notes: Snap beans slow-cooked with bacon or salt pork, onions, and broth until tender — a Southern long-cooked side.

name: Peanut butter brownies
notes: A peanut butter cookie-bar topped with melted chocolate, or chocolate brownies swirled with peanut butter — both eat like a Reese's cup.

name: Cheese grits
notes: Stone-ground grits simmered in water or milk, then folded with butter, eggs, and sharp cheddar — sometimes baked into a casserole.

name: Chocolate chip cheesecake
notes: A baked cream-cheese cheesecake folded with mini chocolate chips, set on a graham or chocolate-cookie crust.

name: Corned beef and cabbage
notes: A brined corned-beef brisket simmered with cabbage, potatoes, and carrots — the Irish-American St. Patrick's Day meal.

name: Beef barbecue
notes: Shredded slow-cooked beef simmered in a sweet-tangy barbecue sauce, served on a soft bun.

name: Soft sugar cookies
notes: A pillow-soft cake-like sugar cookie made tender by sour cream or buttermilk — frosted with vanilla or almond icing.

name: Thumbprint cookies
notes: A buttery shortbread or nut-rolled cookie pressed in the center with a thumb, then filled with jam or chocolate.

name: Cream of mushroom soup
notes: Mushrooms simmered with onion and herbs, blended (or left chunky), and thickened with a milk-and-roux base into a creamy soup.

name: Curry dip
notes: Mayo and sour cream blended with curry powder, lemon, garlic, and Worcestershire — chilled and served with raw vegetables.

name: Chicken gumbo
notes: Chicken simmered in a dark-roux broth with the trinity of vegetables, okra, and andouille sausage — served over rice.

name: Swiss vegetable medley
notes: Frozen mixed vegetables (broccoli, carrots, cauliflower) baked with sour cream, cream of mushroom soup, and Swiss cheese under a buttered fried-onion top.

name: Beef brisket
notes: A tough cut of beef rubbed with seasonings and slowly braised, smoked, or oven-roasted until fork-tender.

name: Onion casserole
notes: Sliced sweet onions baked in butter and cream of mushroom soup under a topping of buttered crackers and shredded cheese.

name: Turkey casserole
notes: Cubed cooked turkey baked with stuffing or noodles, mushroom soup, vegetables, and cheese — a leftover-turkey one-dish meal.

name: Chocolate brownies
notes: A dense fudgy bar of chocolate, butter, sugar, eggs, and a small amount of flour — baked just until the center sets.

name: Shrimp étouffée
notes: Shrimp simmered in a blond-roux base with the trinity of vegetables, Creole seasoning, and shrimp stock, served over rice.

name: Ham roll-ups
notes: Slices of ham spread with cream cheese, rolled around a pickle spear or asparagus, and sliced into pinwheel appetizers.

name: Applesauce cookies
notes: Soft spice-cookies sweetened and made moist by applesauce, often folded with raisins and walnuts.

name: Rhubarb crunch
notes: Chopped rhubarb baked between layers of oat-and-brown-sugar crumble — a tart spring counterpart to apple crisp.

name: Party chicken
notes: Chicken breasts wrapped in bacon or topped with dried beef, baked in sour cream and cream of mushroom soup — a 1960s entertaining classic.

name: Grasshopper pie
notes: A chilled pie of crème de menthe and crème de cacao folded into marshmallows and whipped cream, set in a chocolate-cookie crust.

name: Brown sugar pound cake
notes: A dense pound cake sweetened entirely (or mostly) with brown sugar — caramel-toned and finished with a caramel glaze.

name: Fish chowder
notes: Cubed white fish simmered with diced potatoes, onions, and milk or cream — a New England-style fish soup.

name: Pigs in a blanket
notes: Mini hot dogs (or cocktail wieners) wrapped in crescent-roll dough and baked — a party appetizer.

name: Tortellini soup
notes: Cheese tortellini simmered in a tomato-and-broth base with sausage, spinach, and Parmesan — Olive Garden's "tortellini en brodo" style.

name: Fresh fruit dip
notes: Sweetened cream cheese whipped with marshmallow fluff or vanilla pudding mix — served chilled with sliced fresh fruit.

name: Morning glory muffins
notes: A spiced bran-or-flour muffin folded with grated carrot, apple, coconut, raisins, and walnuts — moist and hearty.

name: Frozen fruit salad
notes: Mixed canned and fresh fruit folded with sweetened cream cheese and whipped topping, frozen in a pan and sliced — a retro Southern dessert.

name: Flan
notes: A baked egg-and-milk custard with sugar caramelized in the bottom of the mold — inverted to serve so the caramel pools over the top.

name: Parmesan potatoes
notes: Halved or quartered potatoes tossed in melted butter and grated Parmesan, then roasted until the cheese forms a crispy bottom crust.

name: Soft molasses cookies
notes: A soft chewy spice cookie of butter, molasses, brown sugar, and warm spices — rolled in sugar before baking.

name: Cranberry nut bread
notes: A holiday quick bread of fresh or dried cranberries, orange zest, and chopped walnuts in a tender batter.

name: Peach ice cream
notes: Custard ice cream churned with ripe pureed peaches and chunks of fresh peach — a Southern summer staple.

name: Sunday brunch bake
notes: A generic egg-and-vegetable casserole or quiche-style bake assembled the night before and baked for Sunday brunch.

name: Bourbon balls
notes: Crushed vanilla wafers mixed with cocoa, powdered sugar, corn syrup, pecans, and bourbon — rolled into balls and dusted in sugar.

name: Potatoes au gratin
notes: Sliced potatoes layered with onions and Gruyère or cheddar in a milk-and-cream sauce, baked until bubbling with a golden cheese crust.

name: Seven layer bars
notes: Graham-cracker crust layered with chocolate chips, butterscotch chips, coconut, and pecans, drizzled with sweetened condensed milk and baked — same as Hello Dollies.

name: Chili beans
notes: Pinto or kidney beans simmered with ground beef, tomatoes, onions, peppers, and chili spices — a softer chili-style stew.

name: Fudge cake
notes: A dense, rich chocolate cake leaning toward brownie texture — moist crumb, deep cocoa, often glazed or frosted with ganache.

name: Flour tortillas
notes: A soft unleavened wheat flatbread of flour, salt, water, and shortening or lard — rolled thin and griddled.

name: Sesame chicken
notes: Battered chicken pieces deep-fried and tossed in a glossy sweet-soy sauce with toasted sesame seeds — Chinese-American restaurant style.

name: Baked fish
notes: White-fish fillets baked in butter, lemon, and herbs until just flaking — a low-effort weeknight preparation.

name: Cowboy beans
notes: Pinto or kidney beans baked with ground beef, bacon, brown sugar, and barbecue sauce — a heartier, sweeter take on chili.

name: Salmon cakes
notes: Canned or cooked salmon mixed with egg, breadcrumbs, lemon, and onion, formed into patties and pan-fried until crisp.

name: Apricot chicken
notes: Chicken pieces baked over apricot preserves whisked with French dressing and onion soup mix — a sweet-savory potluck favorite.

name: Barbecue beans
notes: Canned beans simmered with ground beef, bacon, onions, brown sugar, and barbecue sauce — a thick, sweet cowboy-style bean side.

name: Creamy potato soup
notes: Diced potatoes simmered in broth with onion and bacon, finished with milk and cream — sometimes topped with cheese and chives.

name: Apple muffins
notes: Tender muffins folded with diced apples and cinnamon — sometimes topped with a sugar streusel.

name: Dirt pudding
notes: Vanilla pudding folded with cream cheese, butter, and whipped topping, layered with crushed Oreos — served in cups, often with gummy worms.

name: Caramel apple dip
notes: Cream cheese whipped with brown sugar, vanilla, and toffee bits — served with sliced apples for dipping.

name: Chocolate éclairs
notes: Pâte-à-choux fingers baked hollow, filled with vanilla pastry cream, and topped with a chocolate glaze.

name: Cracker Jack (caramel-peanut popcorn)
notes: Popped corn and peanuts coated in a hot molasses-and-brown-sugar caramel, then baked until crisp.

name: Lime salad
notes: Lime gelatin set with crushed pineapple, cottage cheese, whipped topping, and chopped pecans — a Southern molded dessert salad.

name: Pulled pork
notes: Pork shoulder rubbed with spices and slow-cooked (smoked, braised, or in a slow cooker) until it shreds with a fork, then tossed in barbecue sauce.

name: Boiled custard
notes: A pourable Southern custard of milk, sugar, eggs, and vanilla cooked gently on the stove until thickened — served chilled in mugs.

name: Sour cream enchiladas
notes: Tortillas rolled around shredded chicken or beef and cheese, baked in a creamy sour-cream-and-green-chile sauce topped with more cheese.

name: Sausage and egg casserole
notes: Breakfast sausage browned, layered with bread and cheese, soaked in egg-and-milk custard overnight, and baked until set.

name: Date pudding
notes: A sticky baked pudding-cake of chopped dates folded into a butter-and-brown-sugar batter, served warm with a toffee sauce.

name: Chicken chow mein
notes: Stir-fried chicken with celery, onions, mushrooms, and bean sprouts in a soy-thickened sauce — served over crispy chow mein noodles or rice.

name: Apple crumb pie
notes: A single-crust apple pie topped with a buttery brown-sugar-and-flour crumb streusel in place of a second crust.

name: Chocolate chip oatmeal cookies
notes: Drop cookies of oats, butter, brown sugar, eggs, and chocolate chips — chewier than chocolate chip thanks to the oats.

name: Pimento cheese
notes: Shredded sharp cheddar bound with mayo and diced pimentos, seasoned with cayenne — the Southern "caviar" spread for sandwiches or crackers.

name: Chocolate cherry cake
notes: A chocolate cake mix combined with canned cherry pie filling and eggs, baked and topped with a chocolate-fudge frosting.

name: White fruitcake
notes: A pale fruitcake of butter, eggs, candied pineapple and cherries, coconut, and pecans — lighter and not spiced, unlike the dark holiday fruitcake.

name: Oatmeal pancakes
notes: Pancakes made with rolled oats soaked in buttermilk and folded into a flour-and-baking-soda batter — tender and hearty.

name: German apple cake
notes: A dense oil-and-egg cake layered or studded with apples and spices — typically a single-pan bake with a sugar dust or simple glaze.

name: Brown sugar cookies
notes: Drop or rolled cookies sweetened with brown sugar instead of white — chewy with caramel-toffee notes.

name: Chocolate mayonnaise cake
notes: A cocoa cake using mayonnaise in place of butter and eggs (mayo carries both fat and emulsion) — moist and rich.

name: Macaroni and cheese casserole
notes: Cooked elbow macaroni baked in a milk-and-flour-thickened cheddar sauce under buttered breadcrumbs or more cheese.

name: Broccoli and cheese casserole
notes: Broccoli florets baked with rice, cream of mushroom soup, and cheddar or Velveeta — a Southern potluck side.

name: Pepperoni bread
notes: Frozen bread dough rolled around pepperoni, mozzarella, and Italian herbs, then baked into a sliceable savory loaf.

name: Beef enchiladas
notes: Tortillas rolled around seasoned ground beef and cheese, lined in a pan, covered in red chile sauce and more cheese, and baked.

name: Boston baked beans
notes: Navy beans slow-baked overnight with salt pork, molasses, brown sugar, and mustard in a covered crock — the New England original.

name: Zucchini fritters
notes: Grated zucchini squeezed dry, mixed with egg, flour, and cheese, dropped into oil and pan-fried until golden.

name: Cheese fondue
notes: Gruyère and Emmentaler melted in white wine with garlic, kirsch, and a touch of cornstarch — kept warm over a flame for dipping bread cubes.

name: Grape salad
notes: Halved grapes folded with sweetened cream cheese and sour cream, topped with brown sugar and chopped pecans — a Southern potluck dessert.

name: Watergate cake
notes: A green-tinted pistachio-pudding-and-cake-mix Bundt with chopped pecans and 7-Up — companion of the Watergate (pistachio) salad.

name: Black walnut cake
notes: A buttery layer cake folded with finely chopped black walnuts and frosted with cream cheese icing — earthier than English walnut versions.

name: Chicken parmigiana
notes: Breaded chicken cutlets fried, then baked under marinara and melted mozzarella with grated Parmesan — Italian-American comfort.

name: Pumpkin chiffon pie
notes: Pumpkin custard lightened with gelatin and beaten egg whites, poured into a baked crust and chilled until set — airier than baked pumpkin pie.

name: Cream of potato soup
notes: Diced potatoes simmered with onion and broth, then blended (or partially mashed) and thickened with milk, cream, and butter.

name: Southern fried chicken
notes: Chicken pieces brined or buttermilk-soaked, dredged in seasoned flour, and deep-fried until crisp — the Southern Sunday-supper classic.

name: Turtles (pecan candy)
notes: Pecans arranged in clusters, topped with a soft caramel, then drizzled or dipped in melted chocolate — resembling turtle shapes.

name: Cheeseburger casserole
notes: Ground beef cooked with onions, peppers, and tomato, layered in a pan with cheese and tater tots or crescent dough, baked.

name: Strawberry ice cream
notes: A churned custard of pureed fresh strawberries blended with milk, cream, sugar, and egg yolks — pink and fruity.

name: Vegetable medley
notes: A mix of seasonal vegetables (carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, squash) roasted or sautéed together with butter and seasonings.

name: Peanut butter squares
notes: A no-bake bar of peanut butter, butter, and powdered sugar pressed into a pan and topped with melted chocolate.

name: Squash fritters
notes: Grated yellow squash mixed with egg, flour, and seasonings, dropped into oil and pan-fried until golden.

name: Shoofly pie
notes: A Pennsylvania-Dutch molasses pie with a wet, gooey bottom and a sandy crumb topping baked into a single crust.

name: Champagne punch
notes: Champagne or sparkling wine mixed with fruit juices, brandy, and a sweetener — served from a bowl with citrus floats.

name: Broccoli-cauliflower salad
notes: Raw broccoli and cauliflower florets tossed with bacon, red onion, sugar, and a mayonnaise dressing — broccoli-salad style.

name: Spice cake
notes: A butter cake heavily scented with cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and allspice — often frosted with cream cheese or caramel icing.

name: Chocolate pudding cake
notes: A self-saucing cake — batter poured into a pan, topped with cocoa and sugar, then boiling water, which sinks to form a pudding sauce as the cake bakes.

name: Crabmeat dip
notes: Cream cheese whipped with crab, lemon, and Worcestershire — served chilled or warm with crackers.

name: Beet salad
notes: Sliced cooked beets tossed with vinaigrette and orange or onion — or molded with citrus gelatin in the Southern style.

name: Cranberry punch
notes: Cranberry juice mixed with orange or pineapple juice and ginger ale or sparkling water — a non-alcoholic holiday punch.

name: Irish stew
notes: Lamb or mutton stewed slowly with potatoes, onions, and carrots in a simple broth — traditional Irish farmhouse fare.

name: Broccoli dip
notes: Chopped broccoli baked with cream of mushroom soup, butter, and processed cheese — a hot dip served with crackers or bread cubes.

name: Swedish apple pie
notes: A crustless single-pan apple "pie" with sliced apples on the bottom and a butter-sugar-flour-pecan batter poured on top — bakes into a self-streuseled crust.

name: Gumbo
notes: A Louisiana stew built on a dark roux with the trinity of vegetables, andouille and chicken or shrimp, okra, and Creole seasoning — served over rice.

name: Sausage rolls
notes: Seasoned sausage meat wrapped in puff pastry and baked into golden logs — a British pub snack.

name: Chicken bake
notes: Chicken pieces baked with rice, vegetables, and mushroom or cream-soup sauce — a low-effort one-dish meal.

name: Pecan tarts (tassies)
notes: Mini cream-cheese pastry shells pressed into muffin tins, filled with a brown-sugar-egg-butter custard and chopped pecans, baked into bite-size tarts.

name: Vinegar pie
notes: A Depression-era chess pie made tart with apple-cider vinegar in place of lemon juice — sugar, eggs, butter, flour, and a splash of vinegar baked into a custard.

name: Sweet potato bread
notes: A spiced quick bread of mashed sweet potato, eggs, oil, and brown sugar — folded with raisins or pecans.

name: Snowball cake
notes: Cubes of yellow cake folded with whipped topping and crushed pineapple, set with gelatin in a bowl, and unmolded covered with shredded coconut.

name: Egg salad
notes: Chopped hard-boiled eggs bound with mayo, mustard, celery, and pickle — served as a sandwich filling or on greens.

name: Toll House pie
notes: A pecan-pie-style filling of eggs, butter, sugar, and flour, packed with chocolate chips and pecans — like a giant chocolate chip cookie baked in a pie shell.

name: Fried cabbage
notes: Shredded cabbage sautéed in bacon fat with onions and a touch of sugar, finished with crisp bacon — a Southern side.

name: Black bottom cupcakes
notes: Chocolate cupcake batter topped with a swirl of sweetened cream cheese and chocolate chips — bakes with a cheesecake-like cap.

name: Russian tea cakes
notes: A butter-and-powdered-sugar shortbread folded with finely chopped pecans, baked into balls and rolled twice in powdered sugar — same as snowball cookies.

name: Freezer slaw
notes: Shredded cabbage salted to draw out water, then tossed in a sweet vinegar dressing and frozen — keeps crisp for months in the freezer.

name: Spaghetti carbonara
notes: Spaghetti tossed off-heat with eggs, grated Pecorino, and crisped guanciale or pancetta — the pasta's residual heat sets the egg into a silky sauce.

name: Hot cheese dip
notes: Velveeta or processed cheese melted with Rotel-style tomatoes and chiles — served warm with tortilla chips.

name: Ham balls
notes: Ground ham mixed with ground pork, crackers, milk, and egg, formed into balls and baked in a sweet brown-sugar-and-mustard glaze — Pennsylvania Dutch.

name: Crab quiche
notes: A pastry shell filled with crab, Swiss cheese, eggs, and cream, baked into a savory custard tart.

name: Graham cracker cookies
notes: A no-bake bar of graham crackers topped with a boiled brown-sugar-and-butter caramel, sometimes with chopped nuts.

name: Chocolate chip bars
notes: A sheet-pan version of chocolate chip cookies — same dough pressed into a pan and baked, then cut into bars.

name: Squash patties
notes: Grated yellow squash bound with egg, flour, and onion, dropped into oil and pan-fried into golden cakes.

name: Pot roast
notes: A tough beef cut (chuck or round) seared, then slow-braised with onions, carrots, and potatoes in seasoned broth until fork-tender.

name: Chocolate cheesecake
notes: A baked cream-cheese cheesecake with melted chocolate folded into the batter — dense and chocolaty.

name: Creamed corn
notes: Sweet corn kernels simmered with butter, cream, milk, and a touch of sugar, thickened slightly with flour — a Southern side.

name: Spaghetti and meatballs
notes: Cooked spaghetti topped with marinara and oven-baked or simmered meatballs of beef, breadcrumbs, egg, and Parmesan.

name: Tex-Mex layered dip
notes: A cold layered dip of refried beans, seasoned sour cream, salsa, cheese, lettuce, and olives — served with tortilla chips.

name: Cream cheese pie
notes: A no-bake or lightly baked pie of sweetened cream cheese in a graham crust, topped with fruit, lemon curd, or cherry pie filling.

name: Sweet potato balls
notes: Mashed sweet potatoes formed around marshmallows, rolled in crushed cornflakes or coconut, and baked until crisp — a Southern side-as-dessert.

name: Blueberry crunch
notes: Canned blueberry pie filling and crushed pineapple baked under a yellow-cake-mix and butter streusel with pecans — blueberry dump cake.

name: Ice cream pie
notes: Softened ice cream spread into a chocolate-cookie or graham crust and frozen, topped with whipped cream or fudge sauce.

name: Blueberry coffee cake
notes: A tender butter cake folded with blueberries and topped with a cinnamon-sugar streusel — served with morning coffee.

name: Teriyaki chicken
notes: Chicken pieces marinated or glazed in a soy-mirin-sugar sauce, then grilled or pan-cooked until lacquered — served over rice.

name: Cheesy potato casserole
notes: Frozen hash browns baked with sour cream, cream of chicken soup, and shredded cheese under a cornflake or buttered-cracker topping.

name: No-bake oatmeal cookies
notes: Cocoa, sugar, milk, and butter boiled to a fudge, then stirred with peanut butter and oats and dropped onto wax paper to set.

name: Sour cream sugar cookies
notes: A soft, cake-like sugar cookie made tender by sour cream — rolled and cut or dropped, often frosted with a vanilla glaze.

name: Cheese roll
notes: Cream cheese mixed with cheddar, seasonings, and chiles or pimentos, rolled into a log and coated in chopped pecans or paprika — sliced and served on crackers.

name: Funnel cake (single)
notes: A pancake-like batter drizzled in concentric circles into hot oil, fried crisp, and dusted heavily with powdered sugar — fairground classic.

name: Scalloped tomatoes
notes: Sliced or stewed tomatoes layered with bread cubes, butter, sugar, and herbs and baked until bubbly — sweet-savory Southern side.

name: Salmon ball
notes: Canned salmon mixed with cream cheese, lemon, and seasonings, shaped into a ball and rolled in chopped pecans or parsley — served with crackers.

name: Dirt (cookies and cream dessert)
notes: Crushed Oreos layered with whipped cream cheese, butter, vanilla pudding, and whipped topping — a cousin of dirt pudding.

name: Avocado dip
notes: Mashed avocado mixed with sour cream, lime, jalapeño, and salsa — served chilled with tortilla chips.

name: Italian meatloaf
notes: A ground-beef loaf with Italian breadcrumbs, Parmesan, herbs, and marinara, baked under mozzarella — meatloaf in lasagna-flavor form.

name: Refried beans
notes: Pinto beans simmered then fried with onion and lard or oil, mashed to a creamy paste — a Mexican staple side.

name: Pasta e fagioli
notes: A rustic Italian soup of small pasta and beans in a tomato-and-broth base with garlic, herbs, and a Parmesan rind.

name: Spinach artichoke dip
notes: Chopped spinach and artichoke hearts baked with cream cheese, sour cream, mayo, and Parmesan until bubbling — served hot with bread or chips.

name: Mango salsa
notes: Diced ripe mango, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime — a fresh sweet-spicy salsa served with grilled fish or tortilla chips.

name: Dishpan cookies
notes: A huge-batch drop cookie of oats, coconut, cornflakes (or Rice Krispies), and chocolate chips — mixed in a dishpan to fit it all.

name: Creamy banana pudding
notes: Vanilla pudding folded with sweetened condensed milk and whipped topping, layered with sliced bananas and vanilla wafers — the Southern classic.

name: Fruit pie
notes: A generic name for a sweetened fruit filling baked or chilled into a pastry crust — apple, peach, berry, or mixed fruits.

name: Chicken Kiev
notes: Pounded chicken breast rolled around an herb-and-garlic butter, breaded, and pan-fried or baked — the butter melts into a sauce when cut.

name: French silk pie
notes: A chocolate mousse-style pie of butter, sugar, eggs, and melted chocolate whipped until airy, poured into a baked crust and chilled.

name: Baked oatmeal
notes: Rolled oats combined with milk, eggs, sugar, butter, and cinnamon, baked into a soft cake-like breakfast — served with fruit and cream.

name: Blueberry buckle
notes: A tender butter cake studded with blueberries and topped with a thick streusel — the streusel "buckles" the cake top as it bakes.

name: Impossible pumpkin pie
notes: A blender custard of pumpkin, eggs, milk, sugar, and Bisquick — self-crusts as it bakes, no separate pastry shell needed.

name: Broccoli and rice
notes: Cooked rice tossed or baked with steamed broccoli, butter, cream of mushroom soup, and shredded cheese.

name: Divinity candy
notes: A fluffy, white, nougat-like confection of hot sugar syrup whipped into stiff egg whites with vanilla and pecans — dropped onto wax paper to set.

name: Onion pie
notes: Sliced sweet onions cooked tender, layered in a pastry crust with cheese and herbs, and baked in an egg-cream custard.

name: Ice cream dessert
notes: Softened ice cream layered with crushed cookies and chocolate or caramel sauce in a pan, frozen, and cut into squares.

name: Cherry cheesecake
notes: A baked or no-bake cream-cheese cheesecake topped with canned cherry pie filling on a graham crust.

name: Italian wedding soup
notes: A clear chicken broth with tiny meatballs, acini di pepe pasta, spinach or escarole, and Parmesan — Italian-American banquet starter.

name: Salsa verde
notes: Tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, garlic, cilantro, and lime blended into a tangy green salsa — Mexican style.

name: Crab spread
notes: Cream cheese mixed with lump crab, lemon, Worcestershire, and seasonings — served chilled with crackers.

name: Blueberry dessert
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan-shortbread crust, sweetened cream cheese, blueberry pie filling, and whipped topping.

name: Corn muffins
notes: Cornmeal-and-flour muffins of milk, eggs, butter, and sugar — tender and lightly sweet, often served with butter and honey.

name: Cheese log
notes: Cream cheese mixed with sharp cheddar and seasonings, shaped into a log and rolled in chopped pecans or parsley — served with crackers.

name: Mushroom soup
notes: Sautéed mushrooms simmered with onion, chicken broth, and herbs, blended (or partially) and thickened with milk-and-butter roux.

name: Lemon cookies
notes: A bright lemon-scented butter cookie made with lemon juice, zest, and sometimes a lemon glaze.

name: Stuffed tomatoes
notes: Tomatoes hollowed and filled with seasoned breadcrumbs, herbs, and Parmesan (or tuna salad in cold versions), then baked or chilled.

name: Cheese soufflé
notes: A bechamel base enriched with grated cheese and yolks, lightened with beaten whites, and baked in a hot oven until puffed and golden.

name: Hot dog chili sauce
notes: A finely ground beef sauce seasoned with chili powder, paprika, and a touch of vinegar — spooned over hot dogs in Southern coney-style fashion.

name: Broccoli quiche
notes: A pastry shell filled with an egg-and-cream custard, blanched broccoli, and Swiss or cheddar cheese — a meatless quiche variant.

name: Gingerbread cookies
notes: Rolled spiced cookies of butter, brown sugar, and molasses — cut into shapes (men, houses) and baked crisp, often royal-iced.

name: Cabbage slaw
notes: Shredded cabbage and carrot tossed with a sweet vinegar or mayo dressing — a slimmer name for coleslaw.

name: Sunshine salad
notes: Orange Jello set with crushed pineapple, shredded carrots, and mandarin oranges — a bright molded Southern salad-dessert.

name: Lemon dessert
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan-shortbread crust, sweetened cream cheese, lemon pudding, and whipped topping — same family as Lemon Lush.

name: Mexican wedding cookies
notes: A butter-shortbread folded with finely ground nuts (almonds or pecans), baked into balls and rolled in powdered sugar — Russian-tea-cake family.

name: Tortellini salad
notes: Cooked cheese tortellini tossed with peppers, olives, pepperoni, and Italian dressing — a pasta-salad variant.

name: Hasselback (sliced baked) potatoes
notes: Whole potatoes sliced almost through, drizzled with butter and topped with cheese, baked until the slices fan open and crisp.

name: Impossible coconut pie
notes: A blender custard of eggs, milk, sugar, butter, vanilla, coconut, and Bisquick — self-crusts as it bakes; no pastry shell needed.

name: English trifle
notes: Layered sponge cake soaked in sherry, custard, jam or berries, and whipped cream, assembled in a glass bowl.

name: Chicken paprikash
notes: Chicken pieces browned and simmered in a sour-cream-and-paprika sauce — served over egg noodles or dumplings.

name: Baked custard
notes: Eggs, milk, sugar, and vanilla baked in a water bath until just set — silky and nutmeg-dusted.

name: Ambrosia salad
notes: Mandarin oranges, pineapple, mini marshmallows, shredded coconut, and sour cream or whipped topping — the canonical Southern fruit-salad-dessert.

name: Graham cracker cake
notes: A tender layer cake using crushed graham crackers in place of much of the flour, often filled with pineapple-and-coconut and whipped cream.

name: 7-Up pound cake
notes: A lemon-lime Bundt cake leavened in part by a bottle of 7-Up — soft crumb, citrus-bright.

name: Swedish pancakes
notes: Thin crepe-like pancakes of flour, eggs, milk, and a touch of sugar — rolled with lingonberry jam and whipped cream.

name: Rhubarb crisp
notes: Sweetened chopped rhubarb baked under a crunchy oat-and-butter streusel — tart, juicy, and served warm with ice cream.

name: Twinkie cake
notes: Split Twinkies arranged in a pan with sliced bananas and topped with vanilla pudding and whipped topping — an icebox dessert.

name: Apple nut cake
notes: A spiced oil-based cake folded with chopped apples and walnuts or pecans — moist with a tender crumb.

name: Chicken and broccoli
notes: Cooked chicken and broccoli baked in a mayo-and-cream-of-chicken-soup sauce under cheese and breadcrumbs.

name: Skillet cookies (date balls)
notes: Chopped dates cooked with butter, sugar, and egg in a skillet, then stirred with Rice Krispies, coconut, and pecans — rolled into balls or pressed into bars.

name: Crème brûlée
notes: A baked vanilla-cream custard chilled, then topped with a thin layer of sugar that is torched into a glassy caramel crust.

name: Pinto bean pie
notes: A Southern pie of mashed pinto beans, sugar, eggs, butter, and vanilla baked into a single crust — tastes pecan-pie-like, not bean-like.

name: Pumpkin squares
notes: A pumpkin-pie filling poured over a yellow-cake-mix base, topped with cinnamon-streusel and chopped pecans, baked into bars.

name: Chess squares (ooey-gooey bars)
notes: A yellow-cake-mix base topped with a cream-cheese-egg-and-powdered-sugar layer that bakes into a gooey filling — chess pie in bar form.

name: Oreo cookie dessert
notes: A crushed-Oreo crust topped with sweetened whipped cream cheese, chocolate pudding, and whipped topping — same family as dirt pudding.

name: Taco bake
notes: Layered ground beef, salsa, beans, and cheese baked over tortilla chips or a crescent-dough crust — a Tex-Mex one-pan casserole.

name: Heath bar cake
notes: A chocolate cake poked and saturated with sweetened condensed milk and caramel, topped with whipped topping and crushed Heath bars.

name: Hawaiian cake
notes: A yellow cake topped with crushed pineapple, vanilla pudding, whipped topping, and shredded coconut — chilled before slicing.

name: Cream cheese brownies
notes: Chocolate brownie batter swirled with a sweetened cream cheese layer for marbled, cheesecake-topped fudgy bars.

name: Hot fudge pudding cake
notes: A self-saucing cake — batter spread in a pan, topped with cocoa-sugar and boiling water, baked so the cake rises and a fudge sauce sinks beneath.

name: Jalapeño cornbread (variant)
notes: A skillet cornbread enriched with cheddar, creamed corn, and chopped jalapeños — same as jalapeño cornbread.

name: Green pea salad
notes: Sweet green peas tossed with hard-boiled egg, cheddar, red onion, and bacon in a mayo dressing — a Southern picnic side.

name: Lemon sponge pie
notes: A lemon-custard filling lightened by beaten egg whites baked into a flaky shell — sets into a sponge-cake top over a tangy curd bottom.

name: Million dollar fudge
notes: A long-cooked fudge of evaporated milk, sugar, butter, chocolate chips, and marshmallow creme, mixed with nuts — Mamie Eisenhower's recipe.

name: Pumpkin dessert
notes: A pumpkin-pie custard poured over a yellow-cake-mix base, topped with butter and pecans, baked — same as pumpkin pie cake.

name: Apricot bars
notes: Cooked dried apricots layered between an oat-and-brown-sugar crumble, baked into bars — chewy, tart-sweet.

name: Spinach soufflé
notes: Chopped spinach folded into a cheese bechamel base, lightened with beaten egg whites, and baked until puffed.

name: Icebox rolls
notes: A sweet yeast dough mixed, refrigerated overnight, then shaped and baked into soft dinner rolls — proofed cold for convenience.

name: Tacos
notes: Seasoned ground beef in crisp corn shells (or soft flour tortillas), topped with lettuce, tomato, cheese, and salsa.

name: Peanut patties
notes: A pink Texas candy of sugar, corn syrup, milk, and peanuts cooked to soft-ball and dropped onto wax paper into patties.

name: Fish tacos
notes: Battered or seasoned white fish in soft tortillas with shredded cabbage, crema, and lime — Baja-style.

name: Hot spiced tea
notes: Black tea simmered with orange and lemon juices, cinnamon sticks, and cloves — sweetened and served hot.

name: Chicken stroganoff
notes: Sliced chicken sautéed with mushrooms and onion in a sour-cream-and-mustard sauce — served over noodles or rice.

name: Dirt dessert
notes: Vanilla pudding folded with cream cheese, butter, and whipped topping, layered with crushed Oreos — same as dirt pudding/cake.

name: Sour cream chicken enchiladas
notes: Tortillas rolled around shredded chicken and cheese, baked in a creamy sour-cream-and-green-chile sauce topped with more cheese.

name: Cowboy-style beans
notes: Canned beans simmered with ground beef, bacon, brown sugar, and barbecue sauce — a thick sweet-savory bean side; the generic "Beans" recipe.

name: Three bean salad (3-bean)
notes: Green, kidney, and wax beans tossed with peppers, onion, and a sweet vinegar dressing — chilled overnight.

name: Toffee
notes: Butter and sugar cooked to hard-crack stage, poured into a sheet, topped with melted chocolate and chopped nuts, then broken into shards.

name: Sausage quiche
notes: A pastry shell filled with cooked breakfast sausage, cheese, and an egg-and-cream custard, baked until set.

name: Zucchini bake
notes: Sliced zucchini baked with eggs, cheese, and herbs in a crustless quiche-like dish.

name: Baked rice
notes: Long-grain rice baked in beef or chicken broth with mushrooms, onions, and butter — Texas hands-off rice pilaf.

name: Cream cheese ball
notes: Cream cheese mixed with cheddar, dried beef or ham, peppers, and pineapple, shaped into a ball and rolled in chopped pecans — served with crackers.

name: Fried okra
notes: Sliced okra dredged in seasoned cornmeal and pan- or deep-fried until crisp — a Southern summer side.

name: Chocolate crinkles
notes: Fudgy chocolate cookies rolled twice (granulated then powdered sugar) before baking — the powdered sugar cracks into a "crinkle" pattern as they spread.

name: Lemon delight
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan-shortbread crust, sweetened cream cheese, lemon pudding, and whipped topping.

name: Cincinnati chili
notes: A finely ground beef chili scented with cinnamon, allspice, cocoa, and clove — served over spaghetti and topped with shredded cheese, onions, and beans (the "five-way").

name: Moist chocolate cake
notes: A buttermilk-and-oil cocoa cake brought to extra moistness with hot coffee or hot water in the batter — tall and tender.

name: Mulled cider
notes: Apple cider simmered with cinnamon sticks, cloves, orange, and lemon — a hot non-alcoholic holiday drink (alcoholic versions add rum or brandy).

name: Martha Washington candy
notes: A fondant-style candy of sweetened condensed milk, butter, powdered sugar, coconut, and pecans rolled into balls and dipped in chocolate.

name: Instant Russian tea
notes: A pantry mix of instant tea, powdered Tang, sugar, and warm spices — stirred into hot water; non-alcoholic.

name: Neiman Marcus cake
notes: A yellow-cake-mix base topped with a cream-cheese-egg-and-powdered-sugar layer baked into a gooey "Neiman Marcus bar" — same family as gooey butter cake.

name: Holiday cheese ball
notes: Cream cheese mixed with sharp cheddar, pineapple, peppers, and seasonings, shaped into a ball and rolled in chopped pecans — Christmas-table appetizer.

name: Sausage and rice casserole
notes: Browned sausage baked with rice, chicken broth, mushrooms, peppers, and onions until rice absorbs the liquid.

name: Chipped beef dip
notes: Cream cheese mixed with sour cream and torn chipped (dried) beef, peppers, and onions — baked or served chilled with crackers.

name: Enchilada pie
notes: A layered "stacked" enchilada casserole of tortillas, seasoned meat, enchilada sauce, and cheese, baked lasagna-style.

name: Garlic mashed potatoes
notes: Boiled potatoes mashed with butter, milk or cream, and roasted or simmered garlic — a side dish with subtle garlic warmth.

name: Tzatziki
notes: Strained Greek yogurt mixed with grated cucumber, garlic, dill, lemon, and olive oil — served chilled with pita.

name: Chicken roll-ups
notes: Crescent-roll dough wrapped around a chicken-and-cream-cheese filling, baked, and served with a cream-soup gravy.

name: Persimmon cookies
notes: A soft spice drop cookie made with persimmon pulp folded into a butter batter with raisins or nuts.

name: Pineapple delight
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of graham crust, sweetened cream cheese, pineapple-pudding filling, and whipped topping.

name: Hamburger stew
notes: Browned ground beef simmered with potatoes, carrots, onions, and tomatoes — a stockpot weeknight stew.

name: Barbecue meatballs
notes: Oven-baked meatballs simmered in barbecue sauce or grape-jelly-and-chili-sauce — held warm in a slow cooker for parties.

name: Turkey burgers
notes: Ground turkey patties seasoned and grilled or pan-cooked, served on buns with the usual burger toppings — a leaner burger alternative.

name: Sour cream cornbread
notes: A skillet cornbread enriched with sour cream and creamed corn — moist, slightly sweet, with a tender crumb.

name: Orange sherbet
notes: A frozen dessert of orange juice or concentrate blended with sugar, a small amount of milk or cream, and sometimes egg whites — lighter than ice cream.

name: Oven beef stew (variant)
notes: Cubed beef and root vegetables tossed with tomato juice, tapioca, and seasonings, sealed and oven-braised low for hours.

name: Applesauce muffins
notes: Spiced muffins made tender by applesauce in place of much of the fat — often with raisins or chopped nuts.

name: Yeast biscuits (angel biscuits)
notes: A Southern biscuit leavened with both yeast and baking powder — exceptionally tall and light, also called angel biscuits.

name: Sponge cake
notes: A foam-leavened cake of beaten whole eggs (or separated yolks and whites) folded with sugar and flour — fat-free or lightly enriched.

name: Chocolate covered cherries
notes: Maraschino cherries wrapped in a fondant of butter, powdered sugar, and corn syrup, dipped in chocolate, and aged so the fondant liquefies inside.

name: No peek chicken
notes: Raw rice and chicken pieces sealed in a covered dish with mushroom soup and onion soup mix — baked an hour without lifting the lid.

name: Slush cocktail
notes: Sweetened fruit juices and vodka or brandy frozen in a container, then scooped slushy and topped with lemon-lime soda — a party drink.

name: Cucumber tea sandwiches
notes: Thin-sliced bread spread with seasoned cream cheese or herb butter and topped with cucumber slices — finger sandwiches for tea or bridal showers.

name: Strawberry trifle
notes: Cubes of angel food or pound cake layered with vanilla pudding, sliced strawberries, and whipped topping — assembled in a glass bowl.

name: 1-2-3-4 cake
notes: A classic American butter cake with 1 cup butter, 2 cups sugar, 3 cups flour, and 4 eggs — the easy-to-remember ratio cake.

name: Salsa chicken
notes: Chicken breasts baked in a jar of salsa and topped with shredded cheese — a three-ingredient Tex-Mex weeknight bake.

name: Cherry cheesecake (no-bake)
notes: A no-bake or baked cream-cheese cheesecake topped with canned cherry pie filling — same family as cherry cheesecake.

name: Company casserole
notes: A retro entertaining bake of ground beef, sour cream, cream cheese, tomato sauce, and noodles topped with cheddar — assembled the night before.

name: Mini cheesecakes
notes: Individual cheesecakes baked in muffin tins over a vanilla wafer or graham crust, then topped with fruit pie filling.

name: Jelly roll
notes: A thin sponge cake baked on a sheet pan, rolled while warm with a tea-towel, then unrolled, spread with jam, and re-rolled into a spiral.

name: Apple brownies
notes: A spiced butter-and-brown-sugar bar folded with chopped apples and walnuts — chewy and apple-fragrant, not chocolaty.

name: Blackberry jam cake
notes: A spiced buttermilk layer cake with blackberry jam folded into the batter, often frosted with caramel icing — Appalachian classic.

name: Apple squares
notes: A spiced sheet-pan version of apple cake — moist butter or oil batter folded with chopped apples, cut into squares.

name: Baked potato salad
notes: A hot potato salad of cubed potatoes baked with sour cream or mayo, bacon, scallions, and cheese — loaded-baked-potato flavors in a casserole.

name: Bubble bread (monkey bread)
notes: Pieces of biscuit dough rolled in cinnamon-sugar, layered in a Bundt pan, and baked with brown-sugar-butter syrup — pulled apart to serve.

name: Marinated flank steak
notes: Flank steak marinated in soy sauce, oil, garlic, and a sweetener, then grilled hot and sliced thin across the grain.

name: Pistachio dessert
notes: A no-bake layered dessert of pecan-shortbread crust, sweetened cream cheese, pistachio pudding, and whipped topping.

name: Caesar salad dressing
notes: An emulsion of olive oil, lemon, egg yolk, anchovy, garlic, Parmesan, and Worcestershire — tossed with romaine for Caesar salad.

name: Hawaiian wedding cake
notes: A yellow pineapple cake topped with sweetened cream cheese and whipped topping, finished with coconut and pineapple — similar to pig pickin' cake.

name: Crab imperial
notes: Lump crab folded with a mayo-and-mustard bechamel, mounded in shells or a casserole, topped with buttered breadcrumbs, and baked — a Chesapeake classic.

name: Rocky road candy
notes: Melted chocolate stirred with mini marshmallows and chopped peanuts or almonds, poured to set and cut into squares.

name: Baked chicken salad
notes: Diced chicken bound with mayo, celery, water chestnuts, and almonds, topped with crushed potato chips or cornflakes and cheese, baked until bubbling.

name: Grits casserole
notes: Cooked grits folded with eggs, milk, sharp cheddar, and butter, baked into a fluffy casserole — sometimes with sausage stirred in.

name: Seasoned rice
notes: White rice cooked in broth with butter and seasonings — a base side dish for chicken, beef, or vegetable mains.

name: Yum yum cake
notes: A yellow cake topped with crushed pineapple, vanilla pudding, sweetened cream cheese, and whipped topping — chilled before serving.

name: Hot broccoli dip
notes: Chopped broccoli baked with cream of mushroom soup, butter, and processed cheese until bubbly — served warm with crackers or bread.

name: Brown bread
notes: A steamed or baked molasses-sweetened bread of whole wheat, rye, and cornmeal flours, often with raisins — a Boston/New England tradition.

name: Triple chocolate cake
notes: A chocolate cake mix combined with chocolate pudding and chocolate chips — three forms of chocolate in one Bundt.

name: Shrimp fried rice
notes: Day-old cold rice stir-fried with shrimp, scrambled egg, peas, scallions, and soy sauce — Chinese-American takeout style.

name: Butterscotch cookies
notes: Drop cookies sweetened with brown sugar and butterscotch chips — chewy and caramel-toned.

name: Chocolate zucchini bread
notes: A spiced cocoa quick bread made moist by grated zucchini — folded with chocolate chips for double chocolate.

name: Boston brown bread
notes: A steamed New England bread of whole wheat, rye, and cornmeal with molasses and raisins — cooked in a covered can in a water bath.

name: Chicken spectacular
notes: Cooked chicken baked with wild and white rice, water chestnuts, French-cut green beans, mushrooms, and mayo — a 1970s entertaining casserole.

name: Chocolate bread pudding
notes: Cubed bread soaked in a chocolate-and-cream custard with melted chocolate chips, baked until set — rich and pudding-like.

name: Mexican pizza
notes: Crispy fried or baked tortillas layered with refried beans, seasoned beef, salsa, and shredded cheese — the Taco Bell classic, homemade.

name: Seasoned oyster crackers
notes: Oyster crackers tossed with oil, dill, dry ranch mix, and garlic powder, baked until aromatic — a seasoned party snack.

name: Molasses sugar cookies
notes: Chewy spiced cookies of butter, molasses, brown sugar, and warm spices — rolled in sugar before baking.

name: Coca-Cola salad
notes: A molded gelatin salad of cherry Jello dissolved in hot Coca-Cola, set with crushed pineapple, cherries, and chopped pecans.

name: Dump salad
notes: Cans of fruit (pineapple, mandarin oranges, cherries) dumped together with vanilla pudding and whipped topping — Southern dessert salad.

name: Sour cream raisin pie
notes: A spiced custard pie of sour cream, eggs, sugar, and plumped raisins — sometimes topped with meringue.

name: Sopaipillas
notes: Squares of leavened wheat dough deep-fried until puffy and hollow — served warm with honey, cinnamon-sugar, or savory fillings.

name: Company chicken
notes: Chicken breasts wrapped in bacon, topped with dried beef, and baked in sour cream and cream of mushroom soup — same as party chicken.

name: Spinach squares
notes: Chopped spinach baked with eggs, flour, milk, and cheese in a sheet pan, then cut into bite-size squares as an appetizer.

name: Apple kuchen
notes: A cake-mix-and-butter base topped with sliced apples, cinnamon-sugar, and a sour cream layer — a Pennsylvania Dutch coffee cake.

name: Swiss chicken
notes: Chicken breasts topped with Swiss cheese and cream of chicken soup, blanketed in herbed stuffing mix and butter, and baked.

name: Broccoli supreme
notes: Broccoli baked with eggs, mushrooms, and onion in a cream-of-mushroom sauce under buttered stuffing crumbs and cheese.

name: Chinese pepper steak
notes: Strips of beef stir-fried with sliced bell peppers and onions in a soy-and-ginger sauce — served over rice.

name: Bananas Foster
notes: Sliced bananas sautéed in butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon, flambéed with rum, and served over vanilla ice cream — Brennan's of New Orleans original.

name: Pecan tassies
notes: Mini cream-cheese pastry shells pressed into muffin tins, filled with a brown-sugar-egg-butter custard and chopped pecans — pecan pie in bite-size form.

name: Mock apple pie
notes: A double-crust "apple" pie made entirely from Ritz crackers simmered in lemon-and-cinnamon syrup — a Depression-era pantry deception.

name: Curried chicken salad
notes: Diced cooked chicken bound with mayo and curry powder, mixed with grapes, apples, almonds, and celery — served chilled.

name: Trifle
notes: Cubed cake or ladyfingers layered with pudding or custard, fruit, jam, and whipped cream — assembled in a glass bowl.

name: Burritos
notes: Large flour tortillas wrapped around seasoned meat, beans, rice, cheese, and salsa — Tex-Mex / Mission-style.

name: Manhattan clam chowder
notes: A tomato-and-broth-based clam chowder with diced potatoes, peppers, onions, and bacon — the red, broth-style cousin of New England chowder.

name: Hot milk cake
notes: A foam-leavened cake of beaten eggs and sugar whisked with hot scalded milk and melted butter — moist, fine-crumbed, served plain or with fruit.

name: Tuna burgers
notes: Canned tuna bound with egg, breadcrumbs, lemon, and onion, formed into patties and pan-fried — served on buns with the usual burger toppings.

name: Double layer pumpkin pie
notes: A graham crust topped with a sweetened cream-cheese layer, then a layer of spiced pumpkin pudding — chilled until set.

name: Rhubarb dessert
notes: A rhubarb-and-strawberry filling baked under a yellow-cake-mix-and-butter streusel — a rhubarb dump cake.

name: Peach cake
notes: A spiced butter cake topped with sliced fresh peaches, sometimes finished with a brown-sugar streusel — a German Pfirsichkuchen-style dessert.

name: Black-eyed pea salad
notes: Black-eyed peas marinated with diced peppers, onions, and herbs in Italian dressing — a Tex-Mex twist on three-bean salad.

name: Potato cheese soup
notes: Diced potatoes simmered in chicken broth with onion, then thickened with milk, butter, and shredded cheddar.

name: Chicken tortilla casserole
notes: Layered tortillas, shredded chicken, mushroom soup, salsa or enchilada sauce, and cheese, baked until bubbly — a King-Ranch-style bake.

name: Overnight salad
notes: Lettuce, peas, eggs, bacon, cheese, and red onion layered in a glass bowl, sealed under a mayo-and-sugar topping — chilled overnight before serving.

name: Peanut butter fingers
notes: A baked oat-and-peanut-butter cookie bar topped with melted chocolate and a peanut-butter-powdered-sugar drizzle, then cut into fingers.

name: Baked squash
notes: Sliced yellow squash baked with eggs, butter, and shredded cheese, topped with buttered cracker crumbs or breadcrumbs.

name: Chinese chicken wings
notes: Whole or split chicken wings marinated in soy sauce, ginger, garlic, and sugar, then baked until sticky and bronzed.

name: Honey mustard chicken
notes: Chicken pieces glazed with a sauce of honey, Dijon mustard, butter, and curry powder, baked until caramelized.

name: Hot cross buns
notes: Sweet enriched yeast buns studded with currants or raisins and spices, marked with a flour-paste cross — an Easter / Good Friday tradition.

name: Lima bean casserole
notes: Lima beans simmered tender, then baked with onions, peppers, and cream of mushroom soup under a cheese-and-cracker topping.

name: Pecan sandies
notes: A butter-and-powdered-sugar shortbread cookie folded with finely chopped pecans — sandy, melt-in-the-mouth crumb.

name: Cauliflower soup
notes: Cauliflower florets simmered in chicken broth with onion, blended smooth and finished with milk, cream, and cheese.

name: Cioppino
notes: A San Francisco Italian-American seafood stew of shrimp, scallops, mussels, clams, and white fish simmered in a tomato-and-white-wine broth.

name: Glorified rice
notes: Cooked white rice folded with crushed pineapple, mini marshmallows, and sweetened whipped cream — a Midwestern dessert-salad.

name: Pasta with vegetables
notes: A generic pasta dish — cooked pasta tossed with sautéed vegetables, herbs, and oil or a light sauce.

name: Chocolate drop cookies
notes: Soft cake-like cocoa cookies of butter, sugar, eggs, and buttermilk, often glazed with a chocolate icing.

name: Chocolate chip pound cake
notes: A yellow or chocolate cake-mix-based Bundt with sour cream and chocolate pudding, folded with chocolate chips.

name: Eggplant parmigiana (variant)
notes: Breaded eggplant slices fried, then baked in tomato sauce under layers of mozzarella and Parmesan — same dish as eggplant parmesan.

name: Raisin cake
notes: A spiced butter cake folded with plumped raisins, sometimes with walnuts — moist and warmly spiced.

name: Finger Jello
notes: Concentrated Jello set with extra gelatin so it firms enough to cut into squares and eat by hand — a kids' lunchbox treat.

name: Cherry dump cake
notes: Canned cherry and pineapple pie filling topped with a yellow cake mix, pats of butter, and chopped pecans — baked until streuseled on top.

name: English pea casserole
notes: Sweet green peas baked with mushrooms, hard-boiled egg, cream of mushroom soup, and cheese under a buttered cracker crust.

name: Chocolate fudge cake
notes: A dense, moist cocoa cake leaning toward brownie-like richness, frosted with chocolate fudge or ganache.

name: Cornbread casserole
notes: Cornbread batter mixed with corn kernels, creamed corn, sour cream, and cheese, sometimes layered with ground beef — baked spoon-bread style.

name: White fudge
notes: A vanilla fudge of sugar, sour cream or evaporated milk, and butter cooked to soft-ball and beaten with nuts — chocolate-free.

name: Mexican meatloaf
notes: A ground-beef loaf with crushed tortilla chips, salsa, peppers, and chili spices in place of breadcrumbs, topped with cheese.

name: Noodle kugel
notes: Egg noodles baked in a sweet custard of cottage cheese, sour cream, eggs, butter, sugar, and raisins — the Ashkenazi Jewish noodle pudding.

name: Old-fashioned tea cakes
notes: A simple Southern butter-sugar-flour cookie scented with vanilla and nutmeg — soft and slightly cakey, served with tea.

name: Fresh coconut cake
notes: A white layer cake brushed with coconut milk or fresh coconut water and finished with seven-minute frosting and freshly grated coconut.

name: Peanut butter blossoms (variant)
notes: Peanut butter cookies rolled in sugar and pressed with a Hershey's Kiss as soon as they come out of the oven.

name: Beef roast
notes: A larger cut of beef (chuck, rump, or round) seared and then slow-roasted or braised with vegetables and broth until fork-tender.

name: Cherry squares
notes: A butter cake or shortbread base topped with cherry pie filling and a crumb topping, baked into bars.

name: Chicken and dressing (Southern)
notes: Shredded chicken folded into cornbread dressing with broth, sage, and onions, baked into a casserole — Southern Thanksgiving leftovers.

name: Hershey bar pie
notes: Melted Hershey almond bars folded into whipped cream, poured into a graham crust, and chilled until set.

name: Mexican fruit cake
notes: A one-bowl batter of crushed pineapple, sugar, eggs, flour, and pecans baked into a sheet cake — topped with cream cheese frosting; American despite the name.

name: Cream cheese mints
notes: Cream cheese kneaded with powdered sugar and peppermint extract, pressed into molds or rolled into balls and dusted with sugar — wedding-table candies.

name: Pear salad
notes: Canned pear halves on a lettuce leaf topped with a dollop of mayo and grated cheese — a retro Southern plate.

name: Chicken paprika
notes: Chicken pieces browned and simmered in a sour-cream-and-paprika sauce — served over egg noodles; close cousin of chicken paprikash.

name: Black bean dip
notes: Black beans pureed with cumin, garlic, salsa, and lime — served warm or chilled with tortilla chips.

name: Quesadillas
notes: Flour tortillas folded around melted cheese (often with peppers, chicken, or beef), griddled until golden — served with salsa and sour cream.

name: Hoppin' John
notes: Black-eyed peas simmered with rice, smoked pork (ham hock or bacon), onion, and peppers — a Carolina-Lowcountry New Year's dish.

name: Nuts and bolts (Chex mix)
notes: Chex cereals, pretzels, and mixed nuts coated in a buttery Worcestershire-and-seasoning blend, then baked until crisp — same as Chex party mix.

name: Cornbread dressing (variant)
notes: Crumbled cornbread mixed with sautéed onions, celery, sage, broth, and eggs, baked into the Southern Thanksgiving "dressing".

name: Apple crumble
notes: Spiced sliced apples baked under a buttery flour-and-sugar crumb topping — the British cousin of apple crisp (no oats).

name: Coconut macaroons
notes: Shredded coconut bound with egg whites and sweetened condensed milk, mounded onto sheets and baked until golden.

name: Hot apple cider
